for consulting services (individual consultant)

 

Regional Project Manager 1

 

Contract No. LEARN-IC-NIO-7.13.1

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

URTF Grant No. TF0C5794

 

 BACKGROUND

 

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is implementing projects financed by the World Bank, including: Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (UIHERP) and Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine Program (LEARN) Program and plans to prepare and implement new operations in cooperation with the World Bank (hereinafter referred to as the Operation(s)).

LEARN

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School”” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The total LEARN financing amounts to US$737 mln provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) – US$675,9 mln and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – US$61.1 mln.

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is funded by a US$235 mln credit provided by Bank resources, supported by credit enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT NUMBER 9721-UA). An additional US$150 mln is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (LOAN NUMBER 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT NUMBER 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million. On June 9, 2026, the Loan Agreement (Third Additional Financing for the Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development was signed in the amount of US$286 mln (LOAN NUMBER K019-UA).

 

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT NUMBER TF0C5794).

On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

For this program, “strategic communication and public engagement” refer to three critical aspects of ensuring the effective implementation of education policies and public trust in reforms:

i. Transparency and trust, including timely and clear communication about key initiatives, accessible information for stakeholders, and proactive crisis communication strategies to address concerns and misinformation.

ii. Awareness and outreach, especially the development of targeted campaigns, public information materials, and digital engagement strategies to ensure broad understanding and support for educational transformations among educators, parents, students, and policymakers.

iii. Capacity building in communication, ensuring that education institutions, regional authorities, and key stakeholders are equipped with the necessary tools, guidelines, and skills to effectively communicate and engage with the public regarding policy changes, funding mechanisms, and international support programs.

Effective communication is a key instrument for building trust in education reforms, shaping public perception, and ensuring stakeholder engagement. The Operation of the World Bank is inlined with the Strategic Action Plan and Communications vision of the Ministry.

 OBJECTIVE

 

The objective of this assignment is to manage and coordinate the implementation of NUS reform initiatives within the designated geographical area, ensure effective adaptation of national programs to the regional context, and maintain close cooperation with local education authorities.

 SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Consultant shall provide the following services, including but not limited to:

  • Manages the implementation of NUS reform initiatives in the designated geographical area.
  • Coordinates with local education authorities and stakeholders to ensure effective implementation of the reform.
  • Monitors progress and implementation challenges of the reform at the regional level.
  • Provides feedback on regional adaptation needs and implementation challenges to NIO management.
  • Supports capacity-building activities of regional education institutions.
  • Maintains regular communication with regional stakeholders.

REPORTING

The Regional Managers Coordinator reports to the LEARN Project Coordinator / Co-Coordinator and works under the supervision of the Head of the New Ukrainian School (NUS) Implementation Office. In carrying out their duties, the Consultant works closely with the Deputy Heads of the NUS Implementation Office and the Heads of the relevant functional units to ensure coordinated planning, management, and implementation of communication activities across the NUS reform portfolio.

The Consultant shall submit monthly reports describing the tasks performed, key results achieved, and challenges identified..

 RESOURCES PROVIDED

MoES provides the Consultant with the information necessary to perform his/her assignment in a timely manner. At the same time, the Consultant independently arranges his/her own workplace, including the equipment necessary to perform his/her functions (e.g., PC, communication means and office equipment).

 QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

  • At least 2 years of experience in managing education projects and administering/implementing them
  • At least 1 year of experience in cooperation with national and local authorities
  • At least 2 years of experience in the education sector, preferably in school education
  • Experience in cooperation with international financial or donor organizations
  • High level of English proficiency (upper intermediate or above)
  • Fluency in Ukrainian

Desirable skills and qualifications:

  • Experience in managing education projects
  • Knowledge of the specifics of the regional education system
  • Understanding of project management methodologies
  • Knowledge of the principles and objectives of the NUS reform
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail
  • Excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills
  • Ability to work under conditions of high uncertainty
  • Crisis management experience

 

 DURATION AND PLACE OF WORK

The Consultant shall provide services until 31 August 2028, with the possibility of extending the contract term until the completion of the LEARN Operation.

The Consultant is expected to work on a full-time basis.

Services are planned to be provided in Kyiv, Ukraine. Business trips of the Consultant to other regions of Ukraine may be required to support the implementation of the Operation.

The Consultant may be expected to provide services remotely; however, at the Client's request, he/she shall arrive and/or provide services at the Client's premises as soon as possible.

Contract terms and working arrangements are subject to negotiation.

APPLICATION PACKAGE

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua, Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org and maryna.chubenko@mon.gov.ua  indicating the email subject: " LEARN-IC-NIO-7.13.1: Selection of Regional Project Manager 1: [NAME]".

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time November 24, 2026.

If the Consultant fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the Consultant's application.

TÉRMINOS DE REFERENCIA

FIRMA CONSULTORA PARA APOYAR LA PREPARACIÓN DE SUBPROYECTOS DE ELECTRIFICACIÓN MEDIANTE EXTENSIÓN DE REDES

1. ANTECEDENTES, OBJETO Y ALCANCE

El Gobierno del Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia, a través del Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energías (MHE), por intermedio del Viceministerio de Electricidad y Energías Renovables (VMEER), y ejecutado por la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto del Programa Electricidad para Vivir con Dignidad (UEP PEVD) en coordinación con la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto de la Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (UEP ENDE), impulsa la implementación del proyecto "Mejora del Acceso Sostenible a la Electricidad en Bolivia - Infraestructura Descentralizada para la Transformación Rural (IDTR III)", financiado con el apoyo del Banco Mundial (US$ 125 millones). Este programa constituye uno de los pilares estratégicos más relevantes para la expansión de la frontera eléctrica en el territorio nacional, orientando sus esfuerzos hacia comunidades rurales de alta dispersión geográfica y vulnerabilidad socioeconómica en departamentos como Potosí, Tarija, Santa Cruz, Beni y Pando.

Las áreas de intervención del IDTR III abordan geografías complejas (Amazonía, Chaco, Valles y Altiplano). Diseñar redes eléctricas en estos entornos requiere análisis especializados de servidumbres de paso, coordinación con distribuidoras locales (p. ej., empresas filiales de ENDE) y la optimización topológica de las redes para minimizar caídas de tensión y pérdidas de energía en largas distancias.

La ejecución exitosa de las redes de distribución en media y baja tensión, así como de las infraestructuras asociadas, requiere de una fase crítica de preinversión e ingeniería de detalle. En este contexto, la realización de estudios técnicos, ambientales, sociales y de diseño final para líneas de transmisión y redes eléctricas de electrificación rural resulta indispensable. Para garantizar que los subproyectos cumplan con los estándares internacionales de ingeniería, rentabilidad, sostenibilidad y marcos salvaguardistas socioambientales exigidos por el organismo financiador, la UEP PEVD, en coordinación con la UEP ENDE, requiere la contratación de una Empresa Consultora Especializada. Dicha entidad asumirá la responsabilidad de estructurar los estudios de ingeniería, levantamientos topográficos, diseños de trazo, dimensionamiento electromecánico y la evaluación de impacto ambiental y social necesarios para la posterior licitación y construcción de las obras, en el formato establecido en el Manual de Elaboración y Evaluación de Proyectos de Electrificación Rural (MEEPER 2025), aprobado mediante Resolución Ministerial N° 085-2025.

Los EDTP deberán identificar y evaluar los riesgos e impactos sociales de cada subproyecto, conforme al Marco de Gestión Ambiental y Social (MGAS) y a los Estándares Ambientales y Sociales (EAS) del Banco Mundial aplicables, particularmente EAS1, EAS2, EAS4, EAS5, EAS7 y EAS10, según corresponda, incluyendo los riesgos asociados a Pueblos Indígenas, vulnerabilidad y exclusión, tierras y servidumbres, participación y conflictividad social.

2. DENOMINACIÓN DE LAS PARTES

Para efectos de los presentes Términos de Referencia, se utilizarán de manera uniforme las siguientes denominaciones:

  • Entidad Contratante: la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto IDTR III del Programa Electricidad para Vivir con Dignidad (UEP PEVD), responsible de la etapa de preinversión de los subproyectos, dependiente del Viceministerio de Electricidad y Energías Renovables (VMEER) del Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energías (MHE), revisara la identificación y priorización de los subproyectos.
  • UEP ENDE: la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto IDTR III de la Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (ENDE), titular de los subproyectos, responsable de tramitar y obtener la Licencia Ambiental y las demás licencias, autorizaciones y permisos que requieran los subproyectos, así como de llevar adelante la licitación e implementación de las obras. Revisara todos los productos de la consultoría y aprueba el diseño final. También será el responsable de obtener la certificación de la aplicación en el diseño técnico, de los estándares constructivos de las empresas distribuidoras.
  • Supervisión: el equipo técnico designado por la UEP PEVD en coordinación con la UEP ENDE para el seguimiento, revisión y aprobación de los productos de la consultoría. Los especialistas sociales de la UEP PEVD y de la UEP ENDE revisarán y darán conformidad a los instrumentos y productos sociales antes de considerar completo el EDTP de cada subproyecto y de proceder con la licitación.
  • Consultora: la empresa consultora adjudicada y contratada, responsible únicamente del diseño técnico (E.D.T.P.) final y de la elaboración de toda la documentación de respaldo, incluida la documentación ambiental y social y los Pliegos / Documentos de Licitación de obras en formato del Banco Mundial y de ENDE. La Consultora no es responsable de tramitar ni de obtener licencias, autorizaciones o permisos.
  • Proponente: la empresa consultora que presenta su propuesta durante el proceso de contratación.
  • Empresa Distribuidora: la empresa que opera el servicio de distribución de electricidad en el área del proyecto.

3. OBJETIVO

3.1 Objetivo de la Consultoría

Elaborar los Estudios de Diseño Técnico de Pre inversión (E.D.T.P.) y toda la documentación de respaldo, en los que se establezcan claramente los aspectos técnicos, económicos, sociales y ambientales del proyecto, de manera que permitan tomar una decisión objetiva respecto al uso adecuado de los recursos de inversión, así como los Pliegos / Documentos de Licitación de obras en formato del Banco Mundial y de ENDE para la ejecución de las obras. Cada EDTP deberá demostrar la viabilidad social del subproyecto y asegurar que el diseño incorpore medidas para evitar, minimizar o mitigar impactos sociales y promover el acceso inclusivo a los beneficios, conforme al MGAS y al Plan de Compromiso Ambiental y Social (PCAS).

Los estudios se enmarcarán en el Reglamento Básico de Pre inversión, en el cumplimiento del Art. 6°, establecido en los procesos, procedimientos e instrumentos técnicos del Sistema Inversión Pública y Financiamiento Externo (S.I.P.F.E.).

5. JUSTIFICACIÓN

El Proyecto "Mejora del Acceso Sostenible a la Electricidad en Bolivia (IDTR III)", financiado por el Banco Mundial mediante el Préstamo BIRF N° 96110 por US$ 125 millones, tiene como objetivo ampliar y mejorar el acceso a servicios de electricidad sostenibles en las zonas rurales de Bolivia. Sus metas al cierre, previsto para el 31 de marzo de 2030, incluyen 34.500 nuevas conexiones eléctricas y 107.000 personas con servicio eléctrico nuevo o mejorado. El Proyecto es ejecutado por el Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energías (MHE), a través de la UEP PEVD, dependiente del VMEER, y por la UEP ENDE.

Para avanzar con la implementación del IDTR III, en particular de las inversiones de extensión de redes del Componente 1, es imprescindible contar previamente con una cartera de subproyectos debidamente identificados y con estudios de preinversión aprobados. Sin esta cartera no es posible iniciar los procesos de licitación ni la construcción de las obras, lo que pondría en riesgo el cumplimiento de las metas físicas y del cronograma de desembolsos dentro del plazo de cierre del Proyecto.

En este marco, la UEP PEVD, en coordinación con la UEP ENDE, aún y prioriza la identificación y la elaboración de los estudios de preinversión de los subproyectos de electrificación rural en los departamentos priorizados de Pando, Beni, Santa Cruz, Tarija y Potosí, que comprenden:

a) Identificación de los subproyectos: verificación de comunidades y familias beneficiarias, de la demanda y de la factibilidad de conexión a las redes existentes de las empresas distribuidoras.

b) Diseño técnico: Estudio de Diseño Técnico de Preinversión (EDTP) de cada subproyecto, elaborado conforme al formato y contenido mínimo del MEEPER 2025, incluyendo el cumplimiento del indicador de costo eficiencia (Costo de Inversión/Familia).

 c) Aspectos sociales y ambientales: elaboración de toda la documentación ambiental conforme a la Ley N° 1333 y sus reglamentos, en base a la cual la UEP ENDE tramitará y obtendrá la Licencia Ambiental, así como de los instrumentos exigidos por los Estándares Ambientales y Sociales (EAS) del Banco Mundial en el marco de lo descrito en el MGAS ( como el Diagnóstico Socioambiental, la estructura del PGAS Contratista (PGAS-C), para su posterior desarrollo por el contratista de obra, y los requisitos y medidas ambientales y sociales específicas del subproyecto para los pliegos, con el presupuesto socioambiental detallado, planes ambientales y sociales entre otros) y de las actas de conformidad de servidumbre y de participación de las comunidades.

d) Pliego de licitación: elaboración de los Pliegos / Documentos de Licitación para la ejecución de las obras en formato del Banco Mundial (Documentos Estándar de Adquisiciones – Solicitud de Ofertas para Obras) y de ENDE, con especificaciones técnicas, planos, cómputos métricos, precios unitarios, presupuesto referencial (incluyendo presupuesto socioambiental) y requisitos ambientales y sociales, de modo que la UEP ENDE pueda licitar los subproyectos inmediatamente después de su aprobación.

El MEEPER 2025, aprobado por el Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energías mediante Resolución Ministerial N° 085-2025 de 20 de junio de 2025, que abroga la Resolución Ministerial N° 030-2023, constituye el instrumento técnico de referencia para la elaboración y evaluación de proyectos de electrificación rural. Esta versión fue actualizada en coordinación con las principales empresas distribuidoras del país e incorpora nuevos índices de costo eficiencia, con un factor de ajuste global de 1,53 sobre los valores referenciales de inversión por usuario según piso ecológico. Los subproyectos que se presenten en el marco del IDTR III deben cumplir el contenido mínimo, la documentación y el indicador de costo eficiencia establecidos en el Anexo I del MEEPER 2025 para su evaluación y aprobación.

Por lo expuesto, la presente consultoría resulta indispensable para conformar una cartera de subproyectos técnica, social y ambientalmente viables, listos para su licitación y ejecución, que permita avanzar con la implementación del IDTR III, evitar retrasos, sobrecostos y reformulaciones durante la etapa de construcción, y asegurar el cumplimiento de los compromisos asumidos con el Banco Mundial.

Para efectos de los presentes Términos de Referencia, un subproyecto es socialmente viable cuando, antes de la licitación, se han evaluado los riesgos sociales pertinentes, realizado la participación requerida, identificado y gestionado las tierras y servidumbres, y definido todas las medidas sociales necesarias.

  1. The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration Project (KDEAP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.
  2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include Development of Artificial Intelligence Frameworks for Kenya’s Education System. The assignment is expected to take twelve (12) calendar months from the date of contract commencement.
  3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.icta.go.ke and www.tenders.go.ke/tenders or can be obtained at the address given below.

The Information and Communications Technology Authority through the Program Implementation Unit (PIU) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.  The shortlisting criteria are:

a) Core business and years in business: The consultant shall be registered/incorporated as a consulting firm with core business in research for at least 5 years.

b) Relevant experience: The firm shall demonstrate having successfully executed and completed at least two (2) assignments of similar nature and complexity in a similar operating environment in the last 5 years. AT LEAST ONE (1) of these prior assignments must have specifically involved Artificial Intelligence in Education (AIED), digital competency framework development/adaptation (e.g., UNESCO DigComp / ICT CFT / AI CFT), or national-scale EdTech curriculum reform. Details of similar assignments - Name and address of the client, scope, value, and period should be provided and submitted.

c) Technical and managerial capability of the consulting firm:  The firm shall demonstrate having the requisite technical and organizational capacity to undertake the assignment in the submitted company profile(s).

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and Revised Fifth Edition September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

7. A Consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

8. Further information can be obtained at the address below during the following office hours 0900 and 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400hours) East African Time (EAT) and public holidays.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

National Individual Consultant

Site Engineer (One Position)

 

Title

Site Engineer

Local Recruitment

Expected Start Date

December 9th 2026

Contract Duration

Eight (8) months (December 2026 – August 2027), with possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance, project needs, and availability of funding.

Level of Input

Full-time

Project

Nurturing Early Skills through Technology (NEST) Project

Financing Partner

The World Bank

Hiring Organization

Shanti Volunteer Association (SVA)

Duty Station

Battambang Province (covering project sites in Kos Kralar, Ek Phnom and Thmar Kaul Districts)

Contract Type

Time Based

 

1.  Background

The Nurturing Early Skills through Technology (NEST) Project is funded by the Japan Social Development Fund (JSDF) and administered by the World Bank. The Project is implemented by Shanti Volunteer Association (SVA) in close collaboration with the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS) of Cambodia.

The Project aims to enhance access to and quality of Early Childhood Education (ECE) through the promotion of learning through play and the integration of digital technology in target districts in Cambodia. The Project supports teacher professional development, establishment of an ECE digital resource platform, parental and community engagement, improvement of preschool learning environments through construction and renovation, and implementation of pilot school meal programs.

The Project is implemented in selected districts in Battambang, Banteay Meanchey, and Pailin provinces, targeting public preschools with the objective of strengthening equitable access to quality ECE services for young children aged 3–5 years.

Under Component 2 of the Project, SVA will implement phase 1 of civil works activities, comprising: (i) construction of 8 new preschool buildings, toilets, water tanks and 6 kitchen facilities; (ii) renovation of 17 existing preschool buildings; and (iii) outdoor environment improvements at  25 targeted preschools. These works are spread across three districts in Battambang province and one district in Banteay Meanchey Province, and procured through Request for Bids (RFB) and Request for Quotations (RFQ) methods.

To strengthen day-to-day site supervision during the main construction period, SVA seeks to recruit a Site Engineer based in Battambang Province. The Site Engineer will provide full-time, on-site supervision of the prime contractor(s) at project sites in Battambang Province, under the technical guidance of the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer.

 

2.  Objectives

The objective of this assignment is to ensure that the prime contractor’s civil works at project sites are executed in accordance with the approved drawings, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities (BoQ), and contract requirements, through on-site supervision by the Site Engineer.

Specifically, the Site Engineer will:

  • Provide full-time, day-to-day on-site supervision of the prime contractor’s works at project sites in the assigned province.
  • Ensure quality of materials and workmanship are complied with specification, approved drawing, method statement and schedules.
  • Ensure that the prime contractor executed all work in compliance with approved Environmental and Social(E&S) document
  • Maintain accurate and complete site records, including site diaries, inspection checklists, measurement records, and photo documentation.
  • Provide verified site-level information (progress, quantities, defects) to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer to support progress monitoring, payment certification, and completion.

 

3.  Scope of Work

Under the technical guidance of the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer, the Consultant shall undertake the following tasks at project sites:

a.  Site Mobilization and Pre-Construction

  • Become familiar with the approved drawings, technical specifications, BoQs, contract documents, and contractors’ work programs for each assigned site, and report any discrepancies to the Civil Engineer and SVA Engineer.
  • Participate in site handover to contractors and in pre-mobilization meetings with contractors, school representatives, and the SVA project team.
  • Sites readiness: coordinate with contractor’s supervisor and relevant stakeholders at target schools during contractor mobilization.
  • Prepare and submit updated sites plan including photos
  • Confirm that contractors have mobilized the required personnel, equipment, materials, site signage, and safety arrangements before works begin.

b.  Day-to-Day Site Supervision and Quality Control

  • Conduct full-time, day-to-day supervision of civil works at assigned sites, prioritizing site visits according to construction schedules and critical activities.
  • Inspect and verify key construction stages before contractors proceed (e.g., reinforcement and formwork inspection prior to concreting), using standard inspection checklists.
  • Verify that materials delivered to site comply with approved samples and technical specifications, and reject and record non-compliant materials.
  • Witness and record field and material tests (e.g., concrete slump tests, sampling of concrete test cubes, compaction checks), and follow up on test results.
  • Issue site instructions to contractors on quality and workmanship issues within delegated authority, and refer matters beyond this authority, including design changes and variations, to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.

 

c.  Site Records, Progress Monitoring and Reporting

  • Maintain a site diary for each site, recording daily activities, workforce and equipment, weather conditions, materials delivered, inspections, instructions issued, visitors, and issues.
  • Maintain photo documentation (before, during, and after works) and inspection records for each site.
  • Monitor actual progress against contractors’ approved work programs, and report delays together with proposed corrective measures.
  • Prepare weekly site progress reports and monthly reports, and submit them to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.
  • Participate in regular site meetings and record minutes and agreed actions, as required.

d.  Measurement and Payment Support

  • Verify at sites the actual completed works in Activity Schedule submitted by contractors
  • Prepare measurement sheets and supporting documentation for contractors’ payment applications, for review by the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.
  • Record and report site conditions or instructions that may give rise to variations or claims, with supporting evidence, for review by the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.

e.  Environmental, Social, and Safety Compliance

  • Monitor contractors’ daily implementation of occupational health and safety (OHS) measures, including use of personal protective equipment (PPE), site fencing and barricading, safety signage, safe working at height, and first aid, with particular attention to the safety of children, teachers, and community members at operating preschools.
  • Monitor implementation of E&S mitigation measures at construction sites, including dust and noise control, waste management, drainage, and agreed working hours, in coordination with the E&S Specialist.
  • Monitor contractor compliance with labor management requirements, including workers’ code of conduct and prevention of child labor.
  • Report E&S incidents, accidents, and non-compliance to the E&S Specialist and SVA Project Manager immediately, and in any case within 24 hours, and follow up on corrective actions.
  • Liaise with school directors, School Management Committees (SMCs), and local authorities on site-level matters, and refer community concerns and grievances to the Project Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM).

f.  Completion and Handover

  • Participate in pre-completion and final inspections, and prepare defect (snagging) lists for each site.
  • Monitor rectification of defects by contractors and confirm completion of rectification works.
  • Compile site-level completion documentation, including as-built mark-ups, photo records, test records, and site diaries.
  • Support the handover of completed facilities to schools, School Management Committees (SMCs), and relevant government counterparts.

 

 

4.  Expected Outputs and Deliverables

The following deliverables are expected over the course of the assignment. Timelines are indicative and subject to adjustment based on project implementation progress and construction schedules.

#

Deliverable

Timeline

1

Inception Work Plan and site supervision schedule for assigned sites

Within two (2) weeks of contract signing

2

Site diaries and inspection checklists for each site

Daily (submitted with weekly reports)

Weekly

Monthly

Within 24 hours of occurrence

Prior to practical completion at each site

8

Site completion documentation package and Final Report

Upon practical completion of each site; Final Report at end of contract

5.  Work Supervision

The Consultant will work under the overall supervision of the SVA Project Manager and will receive day-to-day technical guidance from the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer.

The Consultant will coordinate and liaise with:

  • The Civil Engineer and the SVA Engineer to ensure a consistent supervision approach across provinces;
  • PMU members and field staff;
  • The E&S Specialist and other technical consultants engaged under the Project;
  • Contractors, site supervisors, and construction personnel at project sites;
  • School directors, School Management Committees (SMCs), community representatives, and sub-national authorities at project sites.

The Consultant shall submit site records and weekly reports to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer, and monthly reports to the SVA Project Manager through the SVA Engineer, for review and approval. The Consultant shall participate in regular coordination meetings, site meetings, and World Bank supervision missions, as required.

6.  Contract Term and Location of Assignment

The contract period is eight (8) months, from December 2026 to August 2027, with possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance, project needs, and availability of funding.

The Consultant will be engaged as a full-time Individual Consultant (IC) under the NEST Project and is expected to be present at project sites on a daily basis throughout the assignment period.

Key arrangements are as follows:

 

  • Duty Station: Battambang Province (covering project sites in Kos Kralar, Ek Phnom and Thmar Kaul Districts)
  • Contract Modality: The contract will be time-based, with remuneration at a fixed monthly rate for the duration of the assignment.
  • Working Arrangements: Full-time, in accordance with SVA working hours. Work outside regular working hours may be required in line with construction activities, subject to SVA policy.
  • The Consultant is expected to work primarily at project sites and to make their own arrangements for workspace. No office space will be provided by SVA; however, the Consultant may use the SVA Battambang Office for meetings or as required. The Consultant is expected to provide their own computer, smartphone for photo documentation, and personal working equipment.
  • Payment Modality: Payment shall be made on a monthly basis upon submission and approval of monthly reports and agreed deliverables.
  • Travel costs directly related to project implementation and approved by SVA, including daily travel to project sites, will be covered in accordance with SVA travel policy.

7.  Consultant Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Engineering, Architecture, or other relevant technical field. A technical diploma with additional relevant site experience may be considered.

Experience

  • Minimum two (2) years of relevant professional experience in site supervision of building construction and/or renovation works.
  • Hands-on experience in site-level quality control, including stage inspections, material checks, and quantity measurement.
  • Experience in maintaining site diaries, inspection records, and progress reports.
  • Experience in construction of schools or other public or community buildings is an advantage.
  • Experience working on World Bank-financed or other internationally funded projects is an advantage.

Technical Competencies

  • Sound practical knowledge of building construction methods, materials, and quality control at site.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, technical specifications, and Bills of Quantities.
  • Ability to carry out site measurements and quantity verification.
  • Familiarity with occupational health and safety (OHS) requirements and environmental and social compliance in construction settings.
  • Ability to keep accurate records and prepare clear and timely reports.
  • Proficiency in MS Office (Word and Excel); knowledge of AutoCAD is an advantage.
  • Fluency in Khmer is required; working knowledge of English, both written and spoken, is required.

Other Considerations

  • Willingness to reside in or near the assigned province and to travel daily to project sites, including remote rural areas.
  • A valid driving license is required.
  • The Consultant must not hold a government position during the contract period.
  • The Consultant must not have any conflict of interest with contractors engaged under the Project.

(iii) Demonstrated experience in designing roads with public transport facilities;

(v) Experience in conducting watershed studies and dimensioning of stormwater drainage (ditches, aqueducts and bridges);

The Consultancy will have a duration of 8 months, from the effectiveness day of the assignment.

The Government of Balochistan, through the Government of Pakistan, has secured USD $100 Million funded through IDA capital credit financing from the World Bank to implement the Getting Results: Access and Delivery of Quality Education Services in Balochistan (GRADES-B) project. The project is designed to increase girls’ and boys’ enrollment in pre-primary and primary grades, and to improve reading and numeracy proficiency in primary grades, all in project-supported schools.

The GRADES-B project aims to address educational disparities in Balochistan by enhancing access, quality, and equity in education. The initiative focuses on foundational literacy and numeracy, increased enrollment, and sustainable systemic reforms. The proposed project is structured around four components to address systemic challenges in the education sector of the province. They focus on improving access to education and enhancing teaching quality, strengthening data-driven accountability, building resilience to climate change, and introducing emergency preparedness mechanisms to minimize disruptions.

Project Management Unit (here and after as the Client) intends to apply part of the proceeds to cover eligible payments for hiring the services of Consulting Firm for Engagement of a Third-Party Validation (TPV) Firm for Verification of Community-Based School Sites Identified by District Education Groups (DEGs) under GRADES-Balochistan (here and after as the Consulting Firm).

Individualni konsultant e na poziciji privremenog asistenta raditi na poslovima auriranja i sistematske uspostave i/ili zamjene zemljišnih knjiga prema podacima nove izmjere u zemljišnoknjinim uredima i izdvojenim organizacijskim jedinicama navedenih opinskih sudova.

  • Znanje iz oblasti zemljišnoknjinog prava koje se primjenjuje u FBiH.

 

Poeljno je da Individualni konsultant u vrijeme prijavljivanja na oglas posjeduje uvjerenje o poloenom ispitu opeg znanja, strunom ili pravosudnom ispitu izdato od nadlene institucije u F BiH, ali nije eliminatorno.  

Zainteresirani su obvezni uz potpisanu prijavu sa kratkim ivotopisom, sa adresom i obvezno naznaenom e-mail adresom da dostave traene dokumente:

  • univerzitetsku diplomu Pravnog fakulteta – VII stupanj, ili visoko obrazovanje prvog, drugog ili treeg ciklusa po Bolonjskom sustavu školovanja sa najmanje 180 ECTS bodova, te dodatak diplomi/diploma supplement, ako je steena po bolonjskom sustavu studiranja; ili uvjerenje o diplomiranju koje nije starije više od godinu dana od dana sticanja traene strune spreme;

  • Pismo preporuke ili druga slina isprava se uzima u obzir kada sadri sve elemente potvrde ili uvjerenja;
  • Uvjerenje/Potvrde/Certifikati o poloenom kursu ili edukaciji izdate od strane institucija koje se bave obukom za rad na raunaru ili uvjerenje o prijepisu ocjena izdato od strane visokoškolske ustanove.

 

Zainteresirani Individualni konsultanti su duni da dostave dokumentaciju (originale ili ovjerene kopije) kojom potvruju da ispunjavaju potrebne kvalifikacije navedene u ovom Pozivu za izraavanje interesa.

U-22/16 i 61/22), Zakona o stvarnim pravima (SN FBiH br. 66/13, 100/13 i 32/19 – Odluka US) i Pravilnika o postupanju u zemljišnoknjinim stvarima (SN FBiH, br. 5/03, 10/07, 80/11, 6/22 i 101/23).

Nepotpune (prijave bez adrese i kontakt informacija, bez priloenih dokaza o traenim kvalifikacijama), neblagovremene i neuredne prijave nee se uzimati u razmatranje.

Oekivani poetak rada u opinskim sudovima je 01.01.2027. godine, a taan datum ovisit e od datuma završetka procedure. Rok završetka angamana ovisit e od broja zaprimljenih prijavnih listova u opinskom sudu. Rad e se odvijati u navedenim zemljišnoknjinim uredima i izdvojenim organizacijskim jedinicama, a sukladno standardnom radnom vremenu opinskog suda.

Privremeni zemljišnoknjini asistenti e biti odabrani u skladu s procedurama Svjetske banke, objavljenim u priruniku “Pravilnik o nabavkama za zajmoprimce IPF“, rujan 2023, revidiran veljaa 2025. i rujan 2025. godine („Pravilnik“). AVIS D’APPEL PUBLIC A MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Démocratique du Congo a sollicité et obtenu un crédit et un don de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) d’un montant total équivalent à 300 000 000,00 USD en vue de financer le coût du « Projet d’Autonomisation des femmes entrepreneures et une mise à niveau des PME pour la transformation économique et l’emploi (TRANSFORME-RDC)» et se propose d’utiliser une partie des fonds de ce crédit et don pour financer les services des : « Organisations Non Gouvernementales (ONG) Chargées de la mise en œuvre des activités de prévention et réponse aux Exploitations et Abus sexuels/Harcèlement Sexuel (EAS/HS)».

 

  1. Le présent avis d’appel public à manifestations d’intérêt fait suite à l’Avis Général de Passations des Marchés publié sur UNDB le 12 septembre 2022 ainsi que sur les sites de Mediacongo (www.mediacongo.net) et de PADMPME (www.padmpme.cd) respectivement le 13 et 14 septembre 2022 et paru dans le journal « La Prospérité n°5916 » le 14 septembre 2022.

 

  1. Les services comprennent : (i) la réalisation des activités de lutte contre les EAS/HS dans le cadre du Projet TRANSFORME devant prendre en compte et contribuer à la mise en œuvre des principes exigés, (ii) l’actualisation de l’étude d’évaluation des risques et la cartographie des services de VBG dans la zone d’exécution du Projet, (iii) la Formation et sensibilisation, (iv) l’appui aux survivant(e)s d’ EAS/HS, (v) l’appui au mécanisme de gestion de plaintes du projet et (vi) le suivi et l’évaluation des activités d’EAS/HS.

 

Les services prévus au titre de ces contrats sont répartis en deux (2) LOTS DISTINCTS constituant deux (2) MARCHES DISCTINCTS :

 

  • Lot 1 : Lubumbashi (Lubumbashi, Kipushi et Likasi) ; et
  • Lot 2 : Kolwezi (Kolwezi et Tenke Fungurume).

 

  1. Les Termes de Reference (TDR) de la mission peuvent être consultés sur le site web suivant : www.transforme.cd, ou peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

Les consultants intéressés doivent produire les informations sur leur capacité et expérience démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour ces prestations.

  • Avoir une expérience dans la collecte éthique de données sur la prise en charge des survivant(e)s de VBG ;
  • Avoir un code de bonne conduite et une politique interne claire visant la prévention et la réponse du harcèlement, de l’exploitation et de l’abus sexuel, y compris un plan régulier de formation du personnel conforme aux standards minimums du projet ;

The People's Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Development of Turtle Hatchery for conservation for the ultimate objective of this assignment is to facilitate hatchling production for conservation of sea turtles in Sonapara, Cox’s Bazar.

  1. The broad scope of consulting services (“the Services”) includes but not limited to:
  • Inception
  • Situational Report
  • Mid-Term Progress Report
  • Comprehensive Conservation Strategy Report
  • The final report consolidating all Deliverables

 

  1. Objectives

The ultimate objective of this assignment is to facilitate hatchling production for conservation of sea turtles in Sonapara, Cox’s Bazar. The specific objectives are to: (1) understand sea turtle nesting sites’ current situation, threats, and necessary conservation actions in Sonapara; (2) establish and operationalize turtle hatchery; and (3) conduct awareness raising activities.

 

  1. Scope of Work
  1. Conduct an assessment and year-round monitoring of sea turtle nesting at Sonapara Beach

The Consultant will identify and map sea turtle nesting sites and conduct focus group discussions (FGDs) with fishers to identify threats (including bycatch, predation, human disturbance, and habitat degradation). The Consultant will monitor nesting throughout the year to capture seasonal patterns and inform conservation actions. Develop a situational report which will cover: (i) identification and characterization of critical nesting habitats; (ii) migration and population studies using appropriate, ethical methods; (iii) development of an inventory of nesting events and hatching success; (iv) documentation of mortality, nesting frequency, and nest fate; and (v) identification and quantification of sources and levels of threats (including bycatch). The Consultant will prepare a comprehensive conservation strategy report summarizing findings and proposing a Conservation Management Plan (CMP) with actionable, long-term strategies, responsibilities, and a time-bound implementation schedule. The report also summarizes the results of all the activities conducted under this assignment.

 

  1. Establish and manage turtle hatchery

The Consultant will establish a turtle hatchery and guard shed with appropriate equipment and security measures. Nests will be managed for safe in-situ incubation and hatching; where in-situ protection is not feasible, the Consultant will implement ex-situ conservation (egg relocation) following accepted protocols and required permits. The Consultant will deploy guards as needed, control predators (e.g., dogs, crows, and other predatory animals), and prevent egg poaching consistent with legal and ethical standards. The Consultant will maintain records of nests managed, relocation activities, hatching success, and predator control actions.

 

  1. Conduct awareness raising activities

The Consultant will conduct awareness meetings with fisher communities on safe handling and release of entangled turtles. The Consultant will identify turtle egg collectors and hold dialogue with them to reduce poaching and promote stewardship. The Consultant will prepare and post informational signboards at key locations, develop and print a sea turtle information poster or leaflet (1,000 copies), and organize media campaigns around turtle hatchling releases and relevant observances (e.g., World Sea Turtle Day), in coordination with local authorities and community groups.

The Republic of Uzbekistan has applied for financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) of the World Bank Group toward the cost of the Connectivity and Transport Sector Improvement Project (CTSIP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the enhancement of the Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices of JSC “O‘zbekiston temir yo‘llari” and its Group entities, comprising a Double Materiality Assessment (DMA); assessment of sustainability-related financial risks and opportunities, including climate-related physical and transition risks and opportunities; an integrated ESG diagnostic covering governance, strategy, risk management, data and internal controls, and readiness for IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 reporting; targeted implementation of both ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 management systems at three common operational sites, together with capacity transfer and tools for subsequent Group rollout; a Scope 1, Scope 2 and material Scope 3 GHG emissions inventory and an air pollutant emissions assessment for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 reporting years, and development of decarbonization and air pollutant emissions reduction programs; and preparation of a 2025 SASB-aligned Sustainability Report and a 2026 IFRS S1/S2-aligned Sustainability Report, together with strengthening of internal sustainability reporting readiness. The Services also include support for one initial engagement cycle with one ESG rating agency selected and contracted by the Client. The Client shall pay the agency’s fees; the Consultant shall not guarantee a particular rating outcome.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

JSC “O‘zbekiston temir yo‘llari” (the “Client”) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

At least 5 comparable assignments completed during the last 5 years involving the preparation and/or assurance of sustainability reports under SASB, IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards and/or GRI Standards for companies in transport, infrastructure, utilities, energy, extractives, manufacturing or other asset-intensive sectors. This is an addendum to the Procurement Notice ref:- SO-MOTCA-567865-CS-INDV published on 10 November 2026. Please kindly take note of the new submission deadline of November 30th, 2026. All other aspects of the notice remain unchanged.

1.  BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT

The Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation (MoTCA) is implementing the Somalia Infrastructure Development for Access and Jobs, Phase 1 (Stairs2Jobs) Project, financed by the World Bank under the Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA). The Project Development Objective (PDO) of Phase 1 is to increase access to resilient infrastructure and infrastructure sector jobs, and to improve the capacity of select institutions.

MoTCA is responsible for the overall management, coordination, supervision, and implementation of all project activities under the Ministry. This includes ensuring the timely implementation of civil works; the procurement of goods, works, and services; and compliance with applicable environmental and social requirements. The Ministry oversees contractors and supervision consultants to ensure that project activities are implemented in accordance with the required technical, quality, environmental, and social standards. It is also responsible for managing project financial activities in coordination with the EAFD, facilitating the timely processing of payments, and preparing periodic work plans, budgets, progress reports, and other required project documentation.

In addition, MoTCA is responsible for implementing the project’s Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), monitoring and evaluating implementation progress and results, addressing implementation challenges, and regularly reporting project performance, progress, and key issues to the World Bank.

To strengthen the effective management, coordination, and implementation of these responsibilities, MoTCA intends to utilise financing under the Stairs2Jobs Project to recruit a Project Coordinator to support the Ministry in the overall coordination and implementation of project activities.

2.  RESPONSIBILITIES

The PIU Project Coordinator for MoTCA will serve as the focal point for coordination and leadership in the effective planning, implementation, and monitoring of all activities under the Stairs2Jobs Project at the MoTCA level. The Project Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing cross-sectoral project activities, ensuring they are implemented in line with approved project objectives, timelines, and budgets. He or she will facilitate coordination and communication among key stakeholders to ensure smooth and efficient project delivery.

All specific duties and responsibilities are detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR), available on the Ministry’s website at https://motca.gov.so, or upon request via in-person submission or email.

3.  SELECTION CRITERIA

The selection shall be based on the qualifications, experience, and skills of the candidate, followed by an interview. The required qualifications, experience, and competencies include:

  • A master’s degree in transport or aviation management, engineering, infrastructure management, public administration, business administration, accounting, economics, or another discipline directly relevant to infrastructure project implementation, institutional coordination, or public-sector programme management, from a recognised university.
  • A minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in project management, infrastructure implementation, transport, aviation, or public administration — of which at least four (4) years must be in transportation, aviation, or infrastructure development related roles, preferably within an FCV context and/or on donor-funded projects.
  • Certification in one or more of the following areas will be given preference: Transport Operations or Planning (TPP), Infrastructure Project Management, Consulting Engineering (FIDIC), Air Traffic Control (ATC), Aeronautical Information Management/Services (AIM), Communication, Navigation and Surveillance (CNS), Airport Management, or other relevant technical certifications from recognised institutions.
  • Demonstrated experience working with government ministries, departments, and agencies (MDAs), development partners, or multilateral institutions.

4.  REPORTING

The Consultant will report to the Director General of MoTCA and work under the overall guidance of the World Bank Task Team Leaders for the Stairs2Jobs Project.

5.  DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

The MoTCA PIU Project Coordinator shall be contracted for an initial period of one (1) year, renewable subject to a satisfactory performance evaluation by the Ministry, approval by the World Bank, and the availability of project funds.

6.  SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation (MoTCA) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must submit the following:

  • A Curriculum Vitae (CV) including three (3) referees.
  • Copies of certificates of academic qualifications.
  • Copy of passport or ID
  • A cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing — Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2025) (the “Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Country:          Federal Government of Somalia (FGS)

Name of the Project: Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING)

 

Assignment Title: Cybersecurity Expert for National Payment System (NPS)

Project ID:     P501662

Individual/Firm:   Individual Selection

Deadline for submission of EOI: November 30,2026 at 4:00pm

Ref No.   SO-MOF-576060-CS-INDV

 

1. Background: In May 2025, the Federal Republic of Somalia, through its Ministry of Finance (MoF) launched the Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING) project. The project development objective is to promote private sector-led growth and job creation by improving the business-enabling environment, strengthening the financial system, and enhancing access to finance.

The SPRING project is organized around four components (three mutually reinforcing and one supporting): (i) Component 1: Improving the enabling environment for the private sector; (ii) Component 2: Deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity; (iii) Component 3: Enhancing access to finance and resilience for MSMEs; and (iv) Component 4: Project Management. A wide range of activities will be implemented as part of this project to reach its development objective, such as improvements to regulatory/institutional frameworks, the rollout of the digital ID system, financial sector reforms, the creation of a risk-sharing mechanism, and the provision of business development services for micro, small and medium enterprises in select economic sectors, among others.

The MoF received US$105 million from the World Bank, including US$10 million from the Somalia Multi-Partner Fund to implement the SPRING project. As part of this initiative, deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity, MoF intends to apply part of the proceeds from the World Bank to finance the position of Cybersecurity Expert for National Payment System (NPS).

2. Responsibilities: The Cyber Security Expert will provide Cybersecurity Strategy, Governance & Function Establishment; Cyber Risk Management, Compliance & Assurance; Security Architecture, Engineering & Secure Development; Security Operations, Monitoring & Incident Response; Identity, Privileged; Vulnerability Management, Security Testing & Threat Management; Cyber Resilience, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery; Participant, Third-Party & Supply-Chain Security; Security Awareness, Team Capability & Knowledge Transfer; All other specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website link:  https://sps.so/docs/TOR%20for%20Cybersecurity%20Expert%20Terms%20at%20NPS.pdf

3.Skills and qualifications

 Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on the qualifications, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Technology, Network Security, Computer Engineering, or a closely related discipline is required. A Master's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Security, Computer Networks and Security, Information Systems, Technology Risk, or a related discipline is strongly preferred.
  • Minimum 10 years of progressive professional experience in cybersecurity, information security, technology risk, IT governance, or security assurance, with substantial hands-on responsibility in regulated or high-availability environments.
  • At least 5 years of experience in a senior, lead, managerial, or consulting role responsible for information-security governance, cyber-risk management, security operations, or cybersecurity transformation.
  • Demonstrated experience establishing, materially uplifting, or leading an information-security or cybersecurity function, ISMS, SOC/security-monitoring capability, incident-response programme, or comparable enterprise security capability.
  • At least two recognized professional cybersecurity or information-security credential is required, such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, GIAC, ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Implementer/Lead Auditor or Senior Lead Implementer, or an equivalent recognized certification.

4. Duration: The proposed duration for the assignment is Twelve Months (12) calendar months from starts date.

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services and furnish the Curriculum Vitae (CV).

Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport and Telecommunication

 

Terms of Reference

 

for

 

Project Manager

 

Micro Small Medium Enterprises (MSME) and Related Technical Assistance
World Bank / NRPB SPEAR Project – Sint Maarten

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Background and context

Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) constitute approximately 95% of all businesses in Sint Maarten and form the backbone of employment, entrepreneurship, and economic resilience. Recognizing their central role, the Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport and Telecommunication (MinTEATT), through the Department of Economy, Transport and Telecommunication (ETT), is undertaking a comprehensive update of four (4) interrelated MSME-related policies, and the MSME institutional strengthening support programs. These two projects are being implemented under The Sustaining Program Effectiveness and Advancing Resilience (SPEAR) Project, funded by the Government of the Netherlands through the Sint Maarten Reconstruction, Recovery, and Resilience Trust Fund (TF) administered through the World Bank and implemented through the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB)[1].   The Sustaining Program Effectiveness and Advancing Resilience (SPEAR) Project is a strategic initiative led by the Government of Sint Maarten and the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB), with support from the Sint Maarten Trust Fund. It aims to enhance the operational effectiveness of recovery efforts and build long-term institutional resilience. The Trust Fund is governed by a tripartite Steering Committee composed of representatives from Sint Maarten, the Netherlands, and the World Bank, which allocates resources to short-, medium-and long-term recovery and capacity-building initiatives.  SPEAR has the following objectives:

  • Enhance the operational capacity and effectiveness of the National Recovery Program Bureau, and
  • Strengthen the institutional and technical capacity of the Government of Sint Maarten to ensure sustainability of investments.

Scope of Work

This task falls within the second component of SPEAR.

  1. A Policy Consultant or firm is engaged to lead the development of four (4) policy documents: These policies form the foundation of Sint Maarten’s MSME business environment. Updating these policies is essential to reflect the current realities, economic conditions, and evolving dynamics of the local business climate—while also anticipating future needs. At the heart of these policy updates is the goal of fostering a supportive, enabling environment in which entrepreneurs and businesses can thrive and operate efficiently. These revisions aim to strike a thoughtful balance between encouraging economic activity and safeguarding the quality of life, ensuring that Sint Maarten remains a safe, vibrant, and sustainable place to live, work, and do business. The policies are:
  1. The National MSME Policy
  2. The Investment and Diversification Policy
  3. The Residential Economic Policy (REP)
  4. The Beach and Vending Policy

The policy revisions are intended to align and update these policies to reflect current day realities on Island. The update is expected to be informed by data-driven strategies including the proposed World Bank Enterprise Survey[2]. Such data along with the revised policy documents are essential to sustaining progress and achieving inclusive economic growth in the vital Medium Micro and Small Enterprise (MSME) sector in Sint Maarten.  Therefore, the updates, will be critical to ensure alignment between these operational aspects, policy development, MinTEATT priorities, and overall GoSXM priorities.

  1. In parallel to the policy revisions, MinTEATT has requested technical assistance from the ongoing Enterprise Support Project (ESP), funded by the same Trust Fund, to support the execution of the operational aspects of MSME programs. This assistance focuses on institutional strengthening of MSME related institutions including the Sint Maarten Entrepreneurship Development Center (SEDC) and the Chamber of Commerce (COCI). The MSME support areas are:  

 

  1. Governance and Oversight Framework: The objective is to strengthen the Ministry’s oversight and governance of MSME support
  2. Monitoring and Evaluation’ (M&E) framework: Development of an M&E framework for MSME support programs.
  3. Standard Operating procedures (SOPs): Establish SOPs for MSME support programs in key aspects to include basic business training, one-on-one business advisory, and business coaching.
  4. Funding mechanisms for MSME support programs.

Terms of reference for these activities are being developed.

Role of the Project Manager

The Project Manager will be responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the SPEAR Project policy development and the ESP MSME institutional strengthening support programs components. This responsibility includes coordinating with the Policy Consultant and other Consultants hired through ESP, managing project workflow, coordinating with Min TEATT/ETT, facilitating stakeholder engagement and ensuring compliance with all project requirements.   The Project Manager will also be responsible for overseeing the day-to-day execution of the project process; maintaining project timelines; ensuring compliance with Government of Sint Maarten requirements; and facilitating the successful delivery of all project outputs. In this role, the project manager shall organize and supervise the identification, formulation, approval, implementation and completion of all activities under the component and liaise with the Project Implementation Unit at the Ministry of Finance (SPEAR) and National Recovery Program Bureau (ESP). Functional responsibilities for the role include:

  1. Project Management and Coordination
  2. Communication with Relevant Stakeholders
  3. Reporting and Monitoring and Evaluation
  4. Oversight and Quality Management

Under the supervision of the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Finance for overall project coordination and administrative oversight, and of the Ministry of TEATT, through ETT, for policy direction and substantive technical oversight, the Project Manager is expected to perform the following tasks. ETT will guide the policy content, review and validate project outputs, and ensure alignment with the Ministry’s priorities, with final policy approval remaining with the competent authorities:

Project Management and Coordination

  • Oversee the execution of the policy development update process and the development of MSME Support Programs ensuring that activities, deliverables and timelines across both workstreams progress in line with approved plans
  • Coordinate with Policy Consultants to monitor the project’s progress, address challenges, and ensure alignment with project objectives and timelines.
  • Facilitate and participate in regular project meetings with MinTEATT/ETT, NRPB, Ministry of Finance, the Policy Consultant and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Work directly with project counterparts and relevant stakeholders to ensure deliverables fall within the applicable scope and budget. This will involve coordinating with departments within the Government as well as external counterparts, including NRPB, to ensure all aspects of each project are compatible and to clarify specific requirements of each project.
  • Ensure project milestones are achieved on-time and that deliverables meet the required quality standards.
  • Identify and manage project risks, developing mitigation strategies as needed.
  • Manage the project budget, track expenditures and ensure allocated resources are used in accordance with approved plans.
  • Participate as a member of the bid evaluation team during the contracting process.
  • Support the selection of new project staff or consultants as needed.
  • Support the revision process of operational project documents (e.g., project operations manual, procurement plan, and environmental and social management plan), as needed. Participate and/or lead technical meetings with agency counterparts and project participant
  • Regularly supervise and report on project execution progress and budget performance
  • Assist with the preparation of progress reports and actionable information as required by Government to support its reporting commitments to the Council of Ministers, the Trust Fund Steering Committee and the World Bank, as needed.
  • Any other task related to this function that will contribute to the objectives of the project

Communication with Relevant Stakeholders

  • Facilitate communication among government counterparts, NRPB/WB and private sector stakeholders
  • Provide contributions to press releases related to project activities, as needed
  • Consolidate and track feedback and recommendations from stakeholders and develop response matrices with the Policy Consultant.
  • Ensure timely reporting, briefing notes, and updates to the Ministry of Finance and other governing bodies as required.

Reporting and Monitoring and Evaluation

  • Monitor Policy Consultant’s deliverables and work quality, ensuring it adheres to the TOR, timelines and quality standards.
  • Prepare and submit progress reports to relevant stakeholders where applicable (MinTEATT/ ETT, Ministry of Finance World Bank)
  • Submit necessary reports on delays and mitigation strategies/ corrective actions to relevant stakeholders (MinTEATT/ETT, Ministry of Finance, World Bank).
  • With the applicable PIUs (MoF, NRPB) provide inputs to address any complaints submitted through the projects’ Grievance Redress Mechanism (https://nrpbsxm.org/complaints-procedure)
  • Prepare and provide input on SPEAR and Institutional strengthening project required reports.

Consultant Oversight and Quality Management

  • Review Policy Consultant’s inception reports, providing feedback and ensuring alignment with project objectives and MinTEATT/ETT priorities.
  • Review all Annotated Policy Outlines (MSME policy, REP, Investment & Diversification Policy, Beach & Vending Policy), coordinating feedback from MinTEATT and ensuring coherence across the four policies.
  • Review all annotated outlines for the MSME institutional strengthening program support documents to assess quality, identify gaps and ensure that they meet technical and operational standards
  • Conduct quality checks of all policy documents ensuring alignment with Governing Program and National Development Plans (and other applicable documents).
  • Facilitate review and approval processes for all consultant deliverables, coordinating feedback from the  Department Head of ETT, Secretary General, Minister TEATT and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure deliverables submitted are timely and are of professional standard, and incorporate stakeholders input where necessary.
  • Work with the Policy Consultant to assess stakeholder feedback, address identified gaps and incorporate feedback agreed upon by TEATT into the final documents and capacity-building materials. Document the reasons for not incorporating substantive stakeholder comments
  • Verify that consultants’ invoices are supported by appropriate reports, deliverables documentation and evidence of work completed.  

Any other tasks related to the function that will ensure successful completion of the SPEAR Project policy development and the Institutional Strengthening components

 

  • Final Project Completion Report- Documentation of the project including activities, results achieved, challenges, lessons learned and recommendations for implementation and future work.
  • Transition report- Handover documentation including all relevant information for smooth transition and continued implementation.
  • Budget execution reports, stakeholder coordination logs
  • Policy Documents (4),
  • MSME Institutional Strengthening documents (3),

Contract Arrangements and Reporting

The contract duration will be twelve (12) months, from contract signing, with the possibility to extend until June 2028. The successful candidate is expected to reside in Sint Maarten/Saint Martin to support the effective organization and execution of the work and ensure continuous engagement with public sector agencies and local stakeholders.

The Project Manager will report to the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Finance for project administration, financial management and compliance and work in close collaboration with the Department of Economic Transportation and Telecommunication (ETT) for substantive technical oversight, policy direction and review of deliverables

Qualifications and Experience

Minimum Requirements

  • At least a bachelor’s degree in public policy, economics, business administration, project management, or another relevant field.
  • At least 5 years of experience in project management, preferably in the public sector or development projects.
  • Demonstrated skills in results-based project planning, monitoring, and management.
  • Experience coordinating multi-stakeholder processes and facilitating consultation workshops.
  • Prior experience working in Sint Maarten or the Caribbean region.

 

Preferred Requirements

  • A master’s degree in a relevant field is a plus.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent.
  • Experience with MSME development, private sector development, or economic policy projects is a plus.
  • Proficiency in Dutch (spoken and written) is a plus.

 

General Competencies

  • Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities simultaneously.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to anticipate challenges and develop effective solutions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including report writing, presentation, and facilitation abilities.
  • Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills, with demonstrated ability to build relationships and coordinate across diverse groups.
  • Computer literate with high proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project) and project management software.

 

[1]   Which is supporting implementation of the Enterprise Support Project (ESP), funded by the Sint Maarten Recovery and Resilience Trust Fund. ESP’s objective is to support the recovery of and increase resilience of existing and new micro, small, and medium sized enterprises in Sint Maarten.

 

[2]   The Enterprise Survey (ES) is a nationally representative firm-level survey with top managers and owners of businesses in over 160 economies (to reach 180 in upcoming years) that measures businesses’ major constraints, performance (including job creation), and characteristics including innovation and technology, market linkages, access to finance, infrastructure, and more. ES’s comprehensive data and analytical reports enable easy comparisons across economies and time.

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): SY-MOF-547078-CS-INDV

The Ministry of Finance of the Syrian Arab Republic (the “Employer”) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the services of a Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component (Sub-Component 2.2), who will provide high-level strategic leadership and policy direction to the Government of Syria in the design, sequencing, and oversight of the public procurement reform program under the Project, with a view to establishing a modern, transparent, and efficient procurement system aligned with international best practices.

The Technical Lead will lead and coordinate implementation of the procurement reform activities under Sub-Component 2.2 - the new public procurement legal and regulatory framework (replacing the Uniform System of Contracts Law No. 51 (2004)), standard bidding documents, the Single Procurement Portal (SPP), an independent procurement complaints and review system, and the national procurement professionalization and capacity-development program, advising the Ministry of Finance and relevant stakeholders, coordinating with government entities, development partners and the World Bank Task Team, overseeing implementation progress and risk management, and leading the results framework for procurement reform, including key performance indicators and milestones. The assignment will be for an initial period of one (1) year, with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance and project requirements (the contract may be extended to cover the full duration of the Project).

The Technical Lead will work under the overall guidance of the Project Coordinator and the Public Financial Management Reform Coordinating Unit (PFMRCU) within the Ministry of Finance, and will closely coordinate with relevant government entities, the Syria External Assistance Fiduciary Section (SEAFS) and the World Bank Task Team.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Ministry of Finance (through the Public Financial Management Reform Coordinating Unit - PFMRCU) now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). Firms' staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

  1. postgraduate qualifications in procurement, law, public administration, engineering, economics, or a related field, and at least ten (10) years of relevant professional management-focused experience;
  2. proven successful experience in leading and managing technical assistance projects financed by international donors;
  3. experience in public procurement, including demonstrated experience in procurement reform, development of legal and regulatory frameworks, and institutional strengthening (highly desirable);
  4. advanced leadership skills in organizational change and development, with the ability to introduce critical reforms in complex organizational and contextual structures, including in Fragile and Conflict-affected Situations (FCS);
  5. proven experience in coordinating, cooperating and negotiating with high-level government officials, donor partners and multiple local stakeholders; and
  6. fluency in Arabic and English.

 

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers [insert correct title and date of applicable Regulations edition as per the financing agreement] (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Ministry of Finance

Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project

Joul Jammal Street, P.O. Box 13136

Damascus, Syrian Arab Republic
