The Consultant shall report to the Client through the official communication channels indicated by OEAPM/PIU. The Consultant shall ensure that all submissions are clearly identified by deliverable code, title, version, date and status. File names shall include the deliverable code, short title, version and date (YYYYMMDD).

The Consultant shall maintain regular communication with MIRD and OEAPM/PIU and shall provide short progress updates when requested. Any issue that may affect the scope, schedule, data availability, methodology assumptions or quality of deliverables shall be communicated early and recorded in the appropriate project register.

    1. Language of deliverables, reporting process and final submission package

Unless otherwise agreed with the Client, deliverables shall be prepared in English. In addition, the following shall be provided in Romanian: the executive summaries of D2, D4, D7 and D8; the Indicator and Threshold Matrix user-facing labels and map legends; the non-technical summary of the final methodology; and the user-facing texts of the pilot/demonstrator.  The Consultant shall ensure that terminology is consistent across all documents, tables, GIS layers and functional specifications.

Each official submission shall include a transmittal note listing the files included in the package, the version number, the status of the deliverable, the date of submission and any limitations or issues requiring the Client's attention.

The final submission package shall include the final methodology report, technical annexes, calculation examples, indicator and threshold matrix, data architecture, data register, metadata, GIS templates/layers where applicable, functional specification, pilot/validation note, workshop/consultation record, Version Log, Comment Log, Change Log/Change Request records if any, NC/CAPA register if any, internal QA/QC checklist and README file, , plus the Implementation Roadmap and the draft next-phase ToR (Sections 3.10–3.11).

    1. Required formats: DOCX, PDF, XLSX/CSV, GIS files, maps, metadata, calculation annexes and editable files

The Consultant shall provide deliverables in formats suitable for review, future editing, archiving and technical reuse. As a minimum, reports shall be submitted in DOCX and PDF. Tables, registers, matrices and data catalogues shall be submitted in XLSX and, where needed, CSV. GIS layers shall be submitted in reusable formats agreed with the Client, such as GeoPackage, SHP, GeoJSON or other standard formats consistent with the Common Data Standard (Section 3.12 / DR-3).

Maps shall be submitted as static PDF/PNG layouts for reporting and, where applicable, as editable GIS project/layout files. GIS packages shall include metadata, CRS/projection information, attribute dictionaries and data lineage. Calculation annexes may be submitted as XLSX, documented scripts, notebooks or other transparent formats agreed with the Client; where open-source risk engines (e.g. OpenQuake) are used, the input model files shall be part of the calculation annexes so that the Beneficiary can re-run and update the computation.

The Consultant shall avoid proprietary or undocumented data structures that prevent future use by the Beneficiary. Where proprietary software is used, the Consultant shall provide exported open or commonly used formats and sufficient documentation to allow MIRD/OEAPM/PIU or a future service provider to understand and reuse the outputs, together with the upfront licence and lifecycle cost assessment required under Section 3.3.

  1. Key Qualification Requirements

The Consultant shall provide a multidisciplinary team capable of developing a technically sound seismic risk methodology, data architecture, indicators, GIS-ready outputs and functional specification for the interactive map. The proposed team shall include the following Key Experts.

The Consultant may propose additional non-key experts if needed. An IT/software development specialist is not required as a mandatory Key Expert, because the main assignment concerns seismic risk methodology, exposure/vulnerability and GIS/data architecture. However, the IT / Web-GIS Functional Specification and Demonstrator Specialist defined in Section 7.4 is a mandatory non-key position: the position must be filled in the proposed team, with a CV meeting the stated minimum requirements, and is assessed on a responsive/non-responsive basis (not scored).

    1. Key Expert 1 - Team Leader / Senior Seismic Risk Methodology Specialist

The Team Leader / Senior Seismic Risk Methodology Specialist shall coordinate the assignment and shall be responsible for the overall technical quality, coherence and integration of the methodology. The expert shall ensure that the risk model, data architecture, indicators, threshold intervals, functional specification and pilot outputs are consistent and aligned with the requirements of MIRD, OEAPM/PIU and the QAP. The fragility/vulnerability modelling responsibility rests with Key Expert 2 (Section 7.2); the Team Leader integrates and verifies it.

Minimum requirements:

  • university degree in civil engineering, structural engineering, earthquake engineering, disaster risk management, or a closely related field;
  • at least 10 years of professional experience in structural engineering, seismic risk assessment, seismic safety, disaster risk reduction, technical assessment, engineering design or related consultancy services;
  • demonstrated experience in preparing, reviewing or coordinating methodologies, technical specifications, engineering reports, guidelines, risk assessment documents or regulatory-support documents;
  • good understanding of seismic hazard, exposure, vulnerability and risk concepts and their integration into practical risk assessment tools;
  • experience in coordinating multidisciplinary teams and communicating with public authorities, institutional clients or technical reviewers;
  • attestation as certified technical expert in constructions in the Republic of Moldova, or a designer certificate in the relevant field, shall be considered an advantage.
  • experience with Moldovan, Romanian, European or international seismic risk / disaster risk reduction projects shall be considered an advantage.
    1. Key Expert 2 - Exposure, Vulnerability and Seismic Risk Modelling Specialist

The Exposure, Vulnerability and Seismic Risk Modelling Specialist shall support the development of the risk calculation framework, vulnerability/exposure modelling rules, scenario logic and interpretation of risk indicators, and shall be responsible for the development or adaptation of the typology-specific fragility functions (lognormal parameters per Section 3.5). The expert shall ensure that the methodology is scientifically defensible and applicable to the Moldovan building stock and available data conditions.

Minimum requirements:

  • university degree in civil engineering, structural engineering, earthquake engineering, risk engineering, disaster risk management or a closely related field;
  • at least 7 years of professional experience in seismic vulnerability assessment, seismic risk assessment, structural assessment, building typology analysis, disaster risk modelling or related technical consultancy;
  • demonstrated experience with exposure data, vulnerability classes, fragility/vulnerability functions, risk indicators, damage/loss assessment or prioritization methodologies including experience in deriving, calibrating or adapting fragility functions;
  • ability to define assumptions, limitations, uncertainty and data quality implications for seismic risk modelling;
  • experience in using RVS, building stock screening, vulnerability typologies or earthquake risk tools shall be considered an advantage;
  • attestation as certified technical expert in constructions in the Republic of Moldova, or a designer certificate in the relevant field, shall be considered an advantage.
  • ability to work with the Team Leader and GIS/Data Architecture Specialist to ensure consistency between the methodology text, calculation matrices, data tables and map outputs.
    1. Key Expert 3 - GIS, Spatial Data and Data Architecture Specialist

The GIS, Spatial Data and Data Architecture Specialist shall be responsible for the spatial data architecture, GIS templates, attribute structures, map layer requirements, data integration rules, metadata and digital handover package. The expert shall also support the preparation of the functional specification for the interactive map from the GIS/data perspective, including compliance with the Common Data Standard (Section 3.12).

Minimum requirements:

  • university degree in GIS, geography, geoinformatics, urban planning, civil engineering, data management, computer science or a closely related field;
  • at least 7 years of professional experience in GIS, spatial data management, geospatial analysis, map production, data architecture or related services;
  • demonstrated experience with GIS formats such as GeoPackage, SHP, GeoJSON, GeoTIFF, XLSX/CSV and with coordinate reference systems, spatial joins, vector/raster processing and map production;
  • experience in designing data dictionaries, attribute structures, metadata, data quality checks and reusable spatial data packages;
  • ability to translate methodological requirements into map layers, filters, symbology, GIS attributes, export/reporting rules and functional requirements for an interactive map;
  • experience with web-GIS configuration, dashboards, open-source GIS tools or interactive map preparation shall be considered an advantage.
    1. Mandatory non-key expert — IT / Web-GIS Functional Specification and Demonstrator Specialist

This position is mandatory in the team composition (non-key: required and verified for responsiveness, not scored). The specialist shall support the structure and testability of the functional and non-functional requirements, user roles, access tiers, performance expectations and UAT-readiness criteria, and shall configure the pilot/demonstrator (Section 3.8) using web-GIS or equivalent tools. Minimum requirements: degree in computer science, geoinformatics, information systems or a related field; at least 3 years of experience in web-GIS configuration, interactive mapping platforms, dashboards or spatial web applications; demonstrated experience with functional specifications or UAT frameworks for GIS/IT products; experience with open-source web-GIS stacks shall be considered an advantage.

The Consultant may propose non-key experts to strengthen specific components of the assignment. These experts are not mandatory Key Experts and shall be mobilized as needed according to the proposed methodology and work plan.

Seismologist / Hazard Interpretation Specialist may be proposed to support interpretation of hazard inputs, return periods, scenario hazard levels, ground motion parameters and consistency with the seismic hazard methodology developed under Subcomponent 3.1.

Seismic Resilience Policy / DRR and Cost-Benefit Specialist may be proposed to support the buildings-focused seismic resilience strategic framework (Section 3.13), including protection objectives and performance levels, retrofit prioritization logic and the strategic (portfolio-level) cost-benefit perspective. This support is non-key and does not replace the seismic risk and GIS responsibilities of the Key Experts. Minimum profile: a degree in a relevant field (disaster risk management, civil / structural engineering, economics, public policy or a related discipline) and demonstrated experience in disaster or seismic risk-reduction strategy/policy or in cost-benefit / economic analysis of resilience investments.

IT / Web-GIS Functional Specification Support may be proposed to assist with the structure of the functional and non-functional requirements, user roles, access modes, performance expectations, UAT criteria or a simple pilot demonstrator. This support is optional and does not replace the seismic risk and GIS responsibilities of the Key Experts.

QA/QC and Data Management Specialist may be proposed to support internal quality control, checking consistency between reports, tables, maps and GIS files, maintaining the Version Log, Comment Log and Data Register, and preparing the final controlled handover package.

Workshop / Facilitation Specialist may be proposed to support the organization of consultations, preparation of workshop materials, collection of comments and documentation of stakeholder feedback.

Socioeconomic / Statistical Data Specialist may be proposed to support the social-vulnerability module (Section 3.5), including census data processing and aggregation rules.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-2.5-EUE-7-R1 – Senior Expert on Optimizing the Network of Vocational Training Institutions)

 

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

GPE TF0D0613

 

Assignment Title: Senior Expert on Optimizing the Network of Vocational Training Institutions

No. LEARN-2.5-EUE-7-R1

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of this assignment is to provide expert and analytical support to the MoES in coordinating activities for preparing regional plans for the formation of the network of vocational and professional pre-higher education institutions by local authorities, according to the Methodological Guidelines for Forming the Network of Institutions of Vocational and Professional Pre-higher Education, approved by the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine Order No. 216-r of March 4, 2026.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 Kyiv time December 04, 2026.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

Consulting Services (Individual Consultant)

Senior Expert on Optimizing the Network of Vocational Training Institutions

Contract No. LEARN-2.5-EUE-7-R1

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project

GPE TF0D0613

  1. Background

 

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$737 mln  provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) – US$675.9 mln and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – US$61.1 mln.

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million. On June 9, 2026, a Loan Agreement (Third Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) was signed between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (Loan No. K019-UA) in the amount of $286 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

II. OBJECTIVE OF THE TASK

The purpose of this assignment is to provide expert and analytical support to the MoES in coordinating activities for preparing regional plans for the formation of the network of vocational and professional pre-higher education institutions by local authorities, according to the Methodological Guidelines for Forming the Network of Institutions of Vocational and Professional Pre-higher Education, approved by the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine Order No. 216-r of March 4, 2026.

The expert will ensure that each region moves forward with the preparation of regional plans for formation of the network of vocational and professional pre-higher education institutions during the assignment period.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Consultant will provide the following services, including but not limited to:

  • Coordinate engagement with regional teams and support the work of regional working groups;
  • Conduct consultations and working discussions with representatives of regional administrations, education departments, and other relevant stakeholders;
  • Provide guidance on the application of the Methodological Recommendations;
  • Deliver training on the use of analytical dashboards and tools for education network planning;
  • Provide advisory support to regional working groups responsible for developing regional plans for the establishment and optimization of vocational and professional pre-higher education networks, including guidance on the collection, analysis, and interpretation of data related to education networks, demographic trends, and labour market needs;
  • Develop and substantiate strategic recommendations for the optimization of education institution networks;
  • Monitor the progress of regional plan preparation and provide regular reports to the Project team.

IV. REPORTING

The Consultant will report to and cooperate with the Project Coordinator (Co-Coordinator) and work under the supervision of the General Director of the Directorate. For operational matters, the Consultant will coordinate his/her activities with the Head of the World Bank Operations Management Unit, ensuring effective interaction and support during project implementation.

The onsultant will prepare:

  • Monthly reports on services provided within the project execution;
  • Regular progress reports on the work with regions;
  • Analytical notes on the status of regional plans preparation.

V. RESOURCES PROVIDED

The MoES will provide the onsultant with the necessary information in a timely manner to carry out his/her duties. The MoES will also ensure the Consultant has a work station, including the necessary equipment to perform his/her functions (e.g., PC, communication tools, and office equipment).

VI. QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

  • Master’s degree or higher in education, public administration, economics, regional development, sociology, information technology, computer science, applied mathematics, statistics, data science, systems analysis, or another related field;
  • At least 3 years of experience working with government authorities and local self-government bodies;
  • At least 2 years of experience in project management in the education or public administration sector;
  • Knowledge of the regulatory and legal framework in the education sector;
  • Proficiency in English at a minimum level of B1;
  • Fluency in Ukrainian.

Desirable skills and qualifications:

  • Experience working with international organizations providing international technical assistance;
  • Leadership skills and ability to work effectively in a team;
  • Experience in drafting regulatory acts would be an advantage;
  • Strong interpersonal communication and consensus-building skills;
  • Ability to adapt to changing circumstances and priorities;
  • Experience in crisis management would be an advantage.

 

VII. DURATION AND LOCATION

The Consultant shall provide his/her services until  October 30, 2027. The contract may be extended subject to satisfactory performance and mutual agreement between the Consultant and the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine during the Project financing period.

The Consultant is expected to provide services under this Agreement on an ongoing basis throughout its term at a level of engagement equivalent to full-time employment, to the extent necessary to properly perform the tasks specified in the Terms of Reference.

The Consultant shall provide services primarily in Kyiv, Ukraine, and may take business trips to other regions of Ukraine to support implementation of the Project.

 

VIII. DOCUMENTS TO BE SUBMITTED

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org, maryna.chubenko@mon.gov.ua: Selection of the Senior Expert on Optimizing the Network of Vocational Training Institutions: [NAME]».

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time December 04, 2026.

If the candidate fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the candidate’s application.

(CONSULTING SERVICES – SELECTION OF CONSULTING FIRMS)

 

 

Country: Republic of Uzbekistan

 

Implementing Agency: National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan.

 

Project Name: “Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable Populations” (INSON, P504420)

 

Financing Agreement (IDA Credit No. 7555-UZ) / Grant Agreement No. TF C4589-UZ

 

Assignment Title: “Expertise in Prosthetic Devices and Rehabilitation Equipment”.

 

Package Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): UZ-INSON-CS-CQS-2.1.11.

 

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank for the implementation of the project “Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable Populations” (INSON) and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards payment for consulting services under this assignment.

 

The consulting services (the “Services”) include: analysis and revision of the Assistive Products List (APL), including classification and criteria for product selection and prioritization; development of draft and final technical requirements and specifications for priority prosthetic and orthotic devices and rehabilitation equipment, including equipment planned for procurement for rehabilitation centres; development of a short-term rental and reuse model for assistive products, including assessment of service-delivery models, financial and institutional arrangements, operational procedures, model contracts, inventory management and monitoring tools; preparation of documents and recommendations for subsequent implementation of the rental scheme, including a pilot-ready implementation package. The assignment also includes stakeholder consultations, training of 14 regional trainers (30 hours of in-person training), followed by training of 208 district-level specialists (20 hours online in two groups using a cascade model). The Terms of Reference provide for limited operational testing of the proposed pilot approach, where feasible within the assignment timeframe.

 

The overall duration of the assignment is seven (7) months. The international key experts shall spend a cumulative minimum of 40 person-days in Uzbekistan, including field visits to at least two regions.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) are available at the following link:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RJ5N9KGvqRp_M5HlMzSaoXShuIk7jk8d/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104755491226149341341&rtpof=true&sd=true

 

The National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan invites qualified consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested firms shall provide information on their institutional experience and similar completed assignments, indicating the client, country, contract value, start and completion dates, scope of services performed, and the firm’s role, as well as information demonstrating their capacity to perform the assignment. In the case of a joint venture (JV), it shall be specified which JV member performed each similar assignment cited. The criteria for the firm’s qualifications and relevant experience are as follows:

 

  • At least five (5) years of institutional experience in prosthetic and orthotic devices, rehabilitation equipment, assistive technology or rehabilitation service delivery.
  • At least two (2) assignments completed within the last ten (10) years in the above fields, carried out at national level or for an international client.
  • At least one (1) assignment completed within the last ten (10) years involving the development, revision or technical assessment of an assistive products list (APL), product selection and prioritization, or technical/quality assessment of assistive products.
  • At least one (1) assignment completed within the last ten (10) years involving rental, reuse, loan-pool arrangements, refurbishment or maintenance of assistive products, or comparable equipment service-delivery arrangements.
  • At least one (1) completed assignment involving the design and delivery of a structured training/capacity-building programme in two or more locations.
  • Ability to mobilize a qualified team with expertise in prosthetics and orthotics, rehabilitation, assistive technology, APL development, financing and training, with capacity to work in Uzbek and Russian.
  • Experience in Central Asia, the CIS or comparable middle-income health systems is an asset.
  • Experience performing assignments for UN agencies, international financial institutions or national ministries of health or social protection is an asset.

 

At the expressions of interest stage, the qualifications and relevant experience of the firm will be evaluated. Key experts and their curricula vitae (CVs) will not be evaluated at this stage; the relevant information will be requested from the selected firm together with its technical proposal.

 

Interested Consultants are referred to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2023) (the “Procurement Regulations”) concerning conflict of interest. The Consultant (including joint venture members and subconsultants) and its affiliates shall not subsequently participate in procurements of goods, works and non-consulting services arising from or directly related to this assignment, including procurements of assistive products and rehabilitation equipment for which specifications are developed under this assignment, as well as services for the organization and operation of rental points (see Section V of the ToR).

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but must clearly indicate whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (JV) and/or subconsultancy. In the case of a joint venture, its members shall be jointly and severally liable under the Contract.

1. Introduction:

The Government of Samoa has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the SFSRDP P181456 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Central Bank of Samoa invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing consulting services to conduct a diagnostic assessment for a national retail payment switch.

The objective of this assignment is to undertake a diagnostic assessment of Samoa's retail payments ecosystem and evaluate the need, feasibility, and potential design options for establishing a National Retail Payment Switch.

Interested consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

This REOI is being issued for the purpose of establishing a shortlist of qualified consulting firms who will subsequently be invited to submit detailed technical and financial proposals under the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method.

 

2. Background:

The Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) is the monetary authority responsible for maintaining financial stability, managing currency issuance, and overseeing the payment systems in Samoa.

Under the Samoa Finance Sector Resilience and Development project supported by the World Bank, the CBS is pursuing initiatives to strengthen the national payments ecosystem, increase digital financial inclusion, improve payment efficiency, and support the country's broader digital transformation agenda. As electronic payment channels continue to expand across banks, mobile money operators, government agencies, merchants, and consumers, the need for more efficient interoperability arrangements has become increasingly important.

Currently, retail payment transactions may be processed through bilateral arrangements, proprietary networks, or international payment schemes, resulting in potential inefficiencies, higher transaction costs, limited interoperability, and constraints on innovation. A National Retail Payment Switch could provide a shared infrastructure enabling seamless, secure, and real-time interoperability among payment service providers.

Before making investment and policy decisions, CBS seeks the services of a consultancy firm to conduct a comprehensive diagnostic assessment to determine whether a National Retail Payment Switch is necessary, feasible, and economically viable, and if so, to identify the most appropriate implementation model for Samoa

 

3. Objective of the Assignment:

The objectives of the assignment include:

  1. Assess the current state of retail payment systems and interoperability arrangements.
  2. Identify gaps, inefficiencies, and constraints within the existing payment ecosystem.
  3. Evaluate current and future demand for interoperable retail payment services.
  4. Assess the business, technical, operational, regulatory, and financial viability of a National Retail Payment Switch.
  5. Examine alternative interoperability models and determine whether a national switch is the most appropriate solution.
  6. Provide recommendations and an implementation roadmap, if deemed necessary.

 

4. Scope of Services:

The Consultant will be expected to undertake activities including, but not limited to:

Task 1: Inception Phase and stakeholder consultation

Task 2: Assessment of the current payment ecosystem

Task 3: Gap Analysis

Task 4: Assessment of the Need for a National Retail Payment Switch

Task 5: Evaluation of Alternative Models

Task 6: Design Considerations (If a Switch is Recommended)

Task 7: Implementation Roadmap

TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR A CONSULTING FIRM

Currently, retail payment transactions may be processed through bilateral arrangements, proprietary networks, or international payment schemes, resulting in potential inefficiencies, higher transaction costs, limited interoperability, and constraints on innovation. A National Retail Payment Switch could provide a shared infrastructure enabling seamless, secure, and real-time interoperability among payment service providers.

Before making investment and policy decisions, CBS seeks the services of a consultancy firm to conduct a comprehensive diagnostic assessment to determine whether a National Retail Payment Switch is necessary, feasible, and economically viable, and if so, to identify the most appropriate implementation model for Samoa.

 

2. OBJECTIVES

 

The overall objective of this assignment is to undertake a diagnostic assessment of Samoa's retail payments ecosystem and evaluate the need, feasibility, and potential design options for establishing a National Retail Payment Switch.

 

Specific objectives include:

1.  Assess the current state of retail payment systems and interoperability arrangements.

2.  Identify gaps, inefficiencies, and constraints within the existing payment ecosystem.

3.  Evaluate current and future demand for interoperable retail payment services.

4. Assess the business, technical, operational, regulatory, and financial viability of a National Retail Payment Switch.

5.  Examine alternative interoperability models and determine whether a national switch is the most appropriate solution.

6.  Provide recommendations and an implementation roadmap, if deemed necessary.

 

 

3. SCOPE OF WORK

The consultancy firm shall undertake, but not be limited to, the following activities:

Task 1: Inception and Stakeholder Consultation

  • Conduct a kick-off meeting with CBS.
  • Review relevant national policies, legislation, regulations, strategies, and previous studies.
  • Identify key stakeholders including:
    • Commercial banks
    • Mobile money operators
    • Government agencies
    • Payment service providers
    • Merchants
    • Telecommunications providers
    • Consumer groups
    • Development partners
  • Develop a stakeholder engagement plan.
  • Conduct interviews, workshops, and consultations.

 

 
  

 

Task 2: Assessment of the Current Payment Ecosystem

Review and assess, at minimum the:

Market Structure

  • Number and type of payment service providers.
  • Customer adoption and usage trends.
  • Existing payment products and services.

Payment Infrastructure

  • Retail payment systems.
  • Automated clearing arrangements.
  • Card payment networks.
  • Mobile money platforms.
  • Internet and mobile banking systems.
  • Government payment platforms.

Interoperability Arrangements

  • Existing bilateral and multilateral arrangements.
  • Connectivity among market participants.
  • Domestic and cross-border payment linkages.

Payment Volumes and Trends

  • Transaction volumes and values.
  • Channel usage patterns.
  • Cash versus digital payment trends.
  • Future market projections.

 

 
  

 

Task 3: Gap Analysis

Assess challenges and constraints including:

  • Fragmented payment arrangements.
  • Lack of interoperability.
  • Operational inefficiencies.
  • High transaction costs.
  • Customer inconvenience.
  • Limited innovation opportunities.
  • Financial inclusion barriers.
  • Settlement and liquidity risks.

 

The consultant shall identify root causes and quantify impacts where possible.

 

 
  

 

Task 4: Assessment of the Need for a National Retail Payment Switch

 

Conduct a comprehensive assessment addressing at minimum :

Strategic Assessment

  • Alignment with national development objectives.
  • Financial inclusion goals.
  • Digital economy initiatives.
  • Government digitization priorities.

 

Functional Assessment

Potential services supported by a switch, including:

  • Account-to-account payments
  • Instant payments
  • Mobile money interoperability
  • QR code payments
  • Merchant payments
  • Government collections and disbursements
  • Bill payments
  • Agency banking transactions
  • Cross-border payment connectivity

 

Demand Assessment

  • Market demand by consumers.
  • Demand by merchants.
  • Demand by financial institutions.
  • Future growth projections.

 

Economic Assessment

  • Cost-benefit analysis.
  • Transaction cost savings.
  • Efficiency gains.
  • Expected economic impact.

 

 
  

 

Task 5: Evaluation of Alternative Models

Assess and compare alternatives such as:

Option 1 - Maintain current arrangements with incremental improvements.

Option 2 - Enhanced bilateral interoperability model.

Option 3 - Shared interoperability platform.

Option 4 – National Retail Payment Switch.

Option 5 - Regional interoperability arrangements.

 

 

For each option, assess:

  • Cost
  • Benefits
  • Scalability
  • Sustainability
  • Risk profile
  • Governance implications
  • Market readiness

Task 6: Design Considerations (If a Switch is Recommended)

Assess at minimum:

  1. Governance Model
  • Central bank-owned.
  • Industry-owned.
  • Public-private partnership.
  • Independent operator.
  1. Technology Architecture
  • Centralized versus distributed architecture.
  • Real-time payment capabilities.
  • ISO 20022 readiness.
  • API-based integration.
  • Cybersecurity requirements.
  • Business continuity and disaster recovery.
  1. Settlement Arrangements
  • Deferred net settlement.
  • Real-time gross settlement linkages.
  • Hybrid models.
  1. Operational Framework
  • Participation criteria.
  • Pricing model.
  • Operating rules.
  • Risk management framework.
  1. Legal and Regulatory Framework
  • Required regulatory changes.
  • Oversight arrangements.
  • Consumer protection considerations.
  1. Future Readiness
    • Readiness for:
      • ISO 20022 migration.
      • Real-time payments.
      • QR payments.
      • Request-to-Pay services.
      • Proxy addressing services.
      • Digital identity integration
      • Regional interoperability initiatives

 

 
  

 

 

Task 7: Implementation Roadmap

Where applicable, develop:

  • Phased implementation roadmap.
  • Governance and institutional arrangements.
  • Procurement strategy.
  • Capacity-building requirements.

 

 

 

  • Change management strategy.
  • Budget estimates.
  • Key milestones and timelines.
  • Risk mitigation measures.

5. SELECTION METHOD

The consultant will be selected through the “Quality and Cost-Based Selection method” in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement Regulations) of September 2023.

 

 

6. QUALIFICATIONS and EXPERIENCE

Firm Experience

The consulting firm (or eligible joint venture) team shall demonstrate the qualifications outlined below.

1.            Demonstrated experience in assignments of comparable scope, specifically in conducting diagnostics and advisory services for national or regional payment systems, with a focus on retail payment switch design, implementation, or assessment within the last 10 years.

2.            Proven track record in supporting the modernization of payment systems to enhance efficiency, security, and interoperability of digital financial services, including experience with regulatory and supervisory frameworks for payment systems in developing country contexts.

3.            Experience advising central banks, financial sector regulators, or payment system operators on the development, evaluation, or integration of payment infrastructure, including interoperability standards (e.g., API, QR) and digital financial services ecosystems.

4.            Familiarity with financial inclusion strategies and demonstrated capacity to assess payment system use cases that promote access to formal financial services and reduce remittance costs

5.            Documented organizational systems and methodologies for conducting diagnostics, stakeholder consultations, and technical assessments in the context of payment system modernization.

7.            Ability to coordinate with the Central Bank of Samoa and other relevant stakeholders, reflecting experience in multi-institutional environments and government-led financial sector reforms.

The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) (the “Bank”) in the form of a grant (hereinafter called “the Grant”), in the amount of US$60 million, toward the cost of the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase (REGAIN) Project (P181250), approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030.

The Marshalls Energy Company (MEC), as Employer and implementing agency, intends to apply a portion of the proceeds of the Grant to eligible payments under a contract for consulting services to prepare and support an implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions, under Sub-Component 3.1 (Sector Development Assistance) of the REGAIN Project. The assignment shall be carried out in close coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and shall cover all MEC-served systems, including Majuro, Ebeye and the outer islands.

The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise proposing activities to be undertaken in the short, medium, and long term and undertaking them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by focusing on regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course correction to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply (excluding petroleum) in RMI as per the provisions of the EA 2025 and aligned with the National Energy Authority Act, 2025.  Services include, among others:

  • Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall Islands;
  • Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector-related international and national commitments and targets;
  • Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps;
  • Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the Energy sector;
  • Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE;
  • Electricity tariff review and recommendations, building on MEC’s existing tariff methodology and extending it to Ebeye; and
  • Addressing the recommendations by preparing, revising, or aligning the policies, regulations, codes, guidelines, and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions.

The assignment is structured as a lump-sum contract with an estimated duration of 9 months, with an expected start date in January 2027. The selected firm will nominate a multidisciplinary team, including the Key Experts described in the attached TOR, and will report to MEC, coordinating closely with NEA, the World Bank, and other relevant stakeholders.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

Implementation Plan for Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and E-Mobility under the Energy Act, 2025 and National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding Petroleum Provisions – REGAIN Project

1. Background

The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is one of the world's smallest and most isolated nations. The country consists of 29 atolls and 5 low coral islands situated on about 181 square kilometers (km2) of land mass in the Pacific Ocean. Majuro (the nation's capital) and Ebeye, the country's two largest urban centers, account for about 96 percent of the total population, while the remaining inhabitants live on the outer atolls. The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) depends mostly on diesel generation to meet the country's growing electricity needs. The country aims to enhance its energy security through renewable energy generation, improve the reliability of electricity supply, enhance energy efficiency, expand e-mobility, and improve access to electricity. Increased energy resilience will reduce dependence on hydrocarbon fuels, insulate the country from the risks of price rises and supply uncertainties, and equip it with natural disaster-resilient electricity infrastructure.

 

MEC, the state-owned energy utility, generates and provides electricity to Majuro Atoll, serving 55 percent of RMI's population. MEC also manages three mini-grids in Jaluit, Wotje, Rongrong (Majuro Atoll), and Kili Island, the latter having been recently transferred to MEC from the Kili Bikini Ejit (KBE) Local Government. Following the integration of the Kwajalein Atoll Joint Utilities Resources (KAJUR) into MEC, MEC is also responsible for power generation and distribution in Ebeye, together with the water and sewerage services previously provided by KAJUR. MEC is responsible for executing plans to enhance energy security but lacks the capability to conceive and implement them. It lacks the funds required to implement these plans. The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has partnered with the World Bank through the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase Project (REGAIN) – an IDA grant of US$60 million approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030. The REGAIN project aims to increase renewable energy generation and improve access to electricity while reducing reliance on diesel-based generation through funding and technical support.

 

RMI’s Electricity Roadmap targets net-zero greenhouse gas emissions and 100% renewable electricity by 2050. As a small and geographically dispersed island nation, RMI remains highly dependent on imported diesel for electricity generation, exposing the country to high energy costs and vulnerability to global fuel price shocks and supply disruptions. To manage this risk, RMI needs to diversify its electricity supply portfolio by integrating more RE, manage demand growth by promoting efficient electricity use, pursue new business opportunities such as EVs, and monitor and report implementation status to the GRMI for appropriate course correction. Ensuring a reliable, clean, and cost-effective electricity supply is therefore critical to achieving national climate commitments, strengthening energy security, and supporting sustainable socio-economic development. The country lacks the legal, policy, and regulatory framework, institutional capability, and the trained manpower required to achieve these objectives. The GRMI has taken some steps in this direction, such as the notification of the Energy Act 2025, which provides a legal, policy, regulatory, and organizational framework to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply for the benefit of RMI’s economy and citizens and to promote the efficient use of energy and of energy from indigenous sources.

 

Under Sub-Component 3.1 of the REGAIN project (Sector Development Assistance), MEC plans to seek consultancy support from a firm to propose a roadmap and undertake proposed activities for the Implementation of the Energy Act (IEA) 2025.  In the roadmap, IEA shall propose activities to be undertaken in the short, medium, and long term and undertake them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by focusing on regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course correction to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply in RMI.

 

IEA shall be prepared in close coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and MEC.

 

IEA shall take into account all Acts, policies, regulations, studies and current practices relevant to electricity (all RE included), Energy Efficiency, E-mobility and their funding, including but not limited to:

 

  • Energy Act 2025
  • National Energy Authority Act, 2025
  • Recommendations contained in Integrated Resource and Resilience Plan 2024-2034
  • Electricity Roadmap of 2018, which provides a relevant and guiding framework for the sector’s development
  • MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model, prepared by MEC’s Supplemental Management and Operations (SMO) consultant under ADB-funded technical assistance, which covers MEC’s operations prior to the integration of KAJUR and on which the tariff review under Task 6 shall build
  • National Targets and the progress achieved against them to date
  • Relevant energy sector programs and studies of other development partners active in the RMI, in particular the Asian Development Bank (ADB), such as the Energy Transition Project, should be taken into account to ensure coordination and avoid duplication.

 

The assignment will support GRMI, MEC, and NEA in translating the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, into an actionable implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility. The assignment will identify required policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building actions, while excluding provisions related to the petroleum sector. This support aligns with REGAIN’s institutional strengthening objectives and RMI’s need to reduce reliance on diesel, improve energy security, and support the integration of renewable energy.

2. Objectives

The objective of the assignment is to prepare a practical, time-bound implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions, and to support the preparation of priority policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building instruments required for implementation.

 

  • Institutional strengthening for the implementation of RE, EE, and e-mobility provisions.
  • Policy and regulatory framework, guidelines for the development of higher RE integration, EE promotion, and e-mobility uptake.
  • Monitoring and reporting framework for RE, EE, and e-mobility targets, progress, and implementation gaps.
  • Database/reporting arrangements for RE, EE, and e-mobility information.
  • Capacity development strategy for institutions, utilities, and local manpower.

3. Project Description

This assignment is financed by the World Bank under the institutional strengthening and implementation support activities of REGAIN. It will support the policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building measures required to implement the RE, EE, and E-mobility provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025.

4. Implementation Arrangements

 MEC will be the Employer and the contracting authority for this assignment, responsible for approving deliverables and payments. The Consultant may proceed to the next deliverable under MEC's general guidance. NEA, as the statutory authority responsible for regulating the energy sector, shall be responsible for the technical and regulatory approval of policy- and regulation-driven deliverables. MEC, as Employer, retains ultimate authority for administrative and financial approval and for the release of REGAIN project funds, which shall follow NEA's technical sign-off on the relevant deliverable. The responsible ministry and Cabinet shall be consulted where recommendations require policy approval, regulatory adoption, statutory action, budget allocation, or cross-government implementation. MEC shall be responsible for formal approval of all deliverables and payments. The Consultant shall work under the direction of MEC and coordinate closely with:

 

  • MEC management and technical staff
  • REGAIN Project Management Services Consultant, as applicable
  • Project Implementation Unit (PMU) within MEC
  • NEA, the national regulatory body, serving as the regulatory interface between MEC and the Consultant
  • Responsible Ministry and Cabinet on policy formulation
  • World Bank on matters requiring no-objection, reporting, or implementation support
  • ADB and other development partners active in RMI's energy sector, as relevant

Petroleum-sector implementation matters are excluded from this assignment.

5. Scope of Services

The scope of services is limited to the electricity sector, in particular renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility, including relevant non-petroleum legal, policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, enforcement, data, and capacity-building provisions necessary for their implementation. Petroleum sector related provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, are excluded from the assignment. While MEC is the Contracting Employer for the entire assignment, NEA serves as the primary technical Client for Tasks 1, 2, 3, and 7, given their statutory and regulatory content. MEC's approval of these deliverables is administrative and financial and follows NEA's technical acceptance.

 

  • Task 1: Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall Islands

The Consultant shall review and map the existing institutional arrangement, policy, and regulatory framework against the provisions and the directions contained in the Energy Act (EA) 2025 and the National Energy Authority (NEA) Act 2025 (harmonious reading) for the development of Renewable Energy (RE), Energy Efficiency (EE), and E-Mobility (E-MB). The Consultant will propose a strategy to address misaligned or missing institutional arrangements, policies, and regulatory framework.

  1. Review of existing applicable  policies, strategies, plans, and studies in the context of the requirements of EA 2025 and NEA Act 2025,
  2. Identify whether the gap is institutional, policy, or regulatory, whether it will be addressed within the existing framework (alignment/modification), or whether a new framework is to be created, and
  3. Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and Institutional framework to address these gaps.

 

  • Task 2: Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector related international and national commitments and targets

The Consultant will undertake a focused review of the GRMI's international commitments, national targets, initiatives for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, and the progress achieved. The diagnostic and strategic review will include the following:

  1. Discussion with the stakeholders and ascertaining reasons for the shortfall in the envisaged progress,
  2. The Consultant shall review relevant national targets, international commitments, ongoing initiatives, and selected comparable Pacific/SIDS practices for RE, EE, and e-mobility implementation. The purpose of the review shall be to identify practical options for policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-building measures suitable for RMI,
  3. Identification of implementation gaps, in particular critical legal, policy, regulatory, and institutional gaps, which impacted the achievements of these initiatives and targets,
  4. Assess whether these legal, policy, and regulatory gaps stem from implementation shortfall or a missing framework, and
  5. Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and institutional framework to address these gaps.

 

  • Task 3: Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps 

The Consultant will propose a strategy with a time-bound implementation roadmap for addressing the gaps identified in Tasks 1 and 2. The proposed strategy will include the following:

  1. Identification of Implementation gaps, i.e., the framework/provision exists but has not been implemented, or there is a shortfall in its implementation,
  2. Identification of gaps in the existing framework, i.e., the legal, policy, regulatory, or Institutional framework provides for the enabling provision, but it has not been enacted or notified; indicate whether it is a policy, regulatory, or institutional issue,
  3. Identify misalignment (even a section or provision of it) of the policy, regulatory framework, or the institutional framework with the EA 2025 and NEA 2025,
  4. Identification of gaps that cannot be dealt with by the existing framework,
  5. Recommendation of a strategy to deal with these identified gaps. The proposed strategy will indicate the required interventions (legal, policy, regulatory and institutional), their implementation order, the stakeholders responsible for addressing them and the timelines within which these will be addressed (short term- within 3 months, medium term- within 6 months and long term-within 12 months) duly aligned with the statutory timelines provided in the Acts and related policies,
  6. Indicate how the recommended interventions will address the identified gaps.
  7. Indicate the way forward for the gaps which cannot be addressed under the existing legal framework, and
  8. Develop a comprehensive implementation roadmap considering the recommendations made in Task 2 and in this Task, and compile the recommendations.

 

The roadmap should indicate:

  • Short-term actions,
  • Medium-term actions,
  • Long-term actions,
  • Responsible institution,
  • Required decision or instrument,
  • Dependency,
  • Level of priority, and
  • Whether the consultant will draft the instrument under this assignment.
  • Task 4: Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the sector

The Consultant will examine whether the current institutional structure, including its roles and responsibilities, aligns with those prescribed in the Energy Act and is conducive to the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI. The Consultant will examine the following:

  1. Clarity in their role and responsibilities (without any overlap) for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB,
  2. The institutional capacity to lead the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI, such as project planning, design, implementation, operation, and maintenance, and
  3. Recommendations for addressing institutional alignment of roles and responsibilities, capacity gaps, and the coordination mechanism between them for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, taking into account the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC.

 

The Consultant will also assess the skills and the manpower required for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI. The Consultant shall assess:

  1. Manpower and the skills available with all important stakeholders,
  2. Assess the manpower and the skill requirements considering the national targets and the evolving (proposed Roadmap) legal, policy, regulatory and institutional framework for the development of RE, EE and E-MB for the next 5 years,
  3. Indicate the gaps between availability and requirements, and
  4. Prepare a strategy to meet this gap, indicating the number, the skill requirements, and how the required skills will be met (contents of the training, how and where the training will be provided, suggestions for international collaboration, certification).

 

 

 

  • Task 5: Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE

The Consultant will assess the status of the RE database to determine its suitability for publishing a report that records, documents, and shares critical information on RE, EE, and E-MB. The Consultant will:

  1. Evaluate the existing database and identify the missing indicators/information gap/data field necessary for various stakeholders to discharge their roles and responsibilities for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in the country (covering Majuro, Ebeye and the outer island systems),
  2. Recommend formats, information to be gathered, sources of this information, reporting institutions, reporting frequency, and validation process,
  3. Recommend the structure of the report to be published, and
  4. Prepare the first RE encompassing the above recommendations, which NEA can subsequently update and improve upon.

 

  • Task 6: Electricity tariff review and recommendations

The tariff review shall build on, and not duplicate, MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model prepared by the SMO consultant. It shall focus on how that methodology has performed in practice, on areas it did not examine in depth, and on extending it to all systems now operated by MEC, including Ebeye following the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC, which was not covered by the earlier work. The review shall also provide MEC and NEA with a clear, evidence-based rationale and supporting calculations for the recommended tariff options, so that they are well prepared to respond to tariff proposals from policymakers, investors and other stakeholders.

 

The Consultant shall review the existing electricity tariff arrangements and prepare recommendations and an implementation pathway that are consistent with the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025. The Consultant shall, in particular:

  1. Assess the adequacy of the current tariff level, structure, adjustment mechanisms, billing arrangements and related subsidy or compensation mechanisms;
  2. Assess the revenue requirement and efficient cost of electricity service, based on verified utility financial, operational and investment data;
  3. Determine the extent to which prevailing tariffs and practices align with the principles contemplated under the relevant sections of the Energy Act;
  4. Assess tariff implications of planned renewable energy, EE, E-mobility, battery storage, network, resilience and access investments;
  5. Recommend refinements to the existing tariff methodology, tariff structure, adjustment mechanism and regulatory review process that NEA can use in tariff determinations;
  6. Review the application of MEC’s current tariff methodology and identify any issues, anomalies or unintended outcomes that have emerged in practice and that may require adjustment;
  7. Extend the revenue-requirement and cost-of-supply analysis to Ebeye following the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC, including harmonization of KAJUR’s financial, operational and customer data with MEC’s, clear separation of electricity costs from water and sewerage costs, and options and a transition pathway for bringing Ebeye’s electricity tariff into MEC’s tariff framework;
  8. Assess the merits and implications of the planned introduction of a single tariff for all customer classes;
  9. Assess whether a uniform national tariff should be maintained across all MEC-served systems (Majuro, Ebeye and the outer islands), or whether location-specific tariffs or tariff adjustment factors are warranted, including the resulting cross-subsidies between locations;
  10. Using the known sizes and costs of the hybrid and mini-grid systems to be installed in the outer islands, estimate the indicative cost of supply and potential tariff for each location, and assess the implications of any proposal to reduce tariffs in locations with high renewable energy penetration;
  11. Assess the practicality, timing and customer impact of reducing or removing existing government subsidies, and the alternatives available;
  12. Assess the feasibility of time-of-use tariffs that reflect the different costs of daytime (predominantly solar) and nighttime (predominantly diesel) supply;
  13. Recommend tariffs and charging arrangements for electric vehicle charging;
  14. Assess feed-in tariff, net-metering and power purchase arrangements for privately owned renewable energy systems seeking to export to MEC’s grid, including pricing based on avoided cost, the grid integration, storage and backup costs borne by MEC, and the volume of such generation the grid can accommodate;
  15. Assess the implications of electricity supplied by third parties outside MEC’s networks, such as renewable energy systems at government or private facilities that supply neighboring communities, including the pricing basis and regulatory requirements for such supply, and how differences between their prices and cost-reflective MEC tariffs can be explained and managed;
  16. Assess distributional and affordability implications for customer classes, including vulnerable customers, and identify transparent options for any subsidy or compensation that may be required; and
  17. Provide practical inputs for preparation and future implementation of the National Electricity Tariff and Billing Code.

 

  • Task 7: Addressing the recommendations

Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap under Task 3, and working under the technical supervision of NEA, the Consultant shall identify, prepare, revise or align the policies, regulations, codes, guidelines and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions.

The Consultant shall, in particular:

  1. Prepare or align the electricity-sector regulatory instruments identified as necessary under the Acts, including, as applicable, electricity licensing, electricity-sector regulation, Grid Code, service standards, universal service and subsidy-related mechanisms,
  2. Prepare or align the instruments required for renewable energy, including, as applicable, grid integration, renewable IPPs, community renewable-energy projects, rooftop installations and renewable microgrids,
  3. Prepare or align the instruments required for energy efficiency, including applicable standards, labeling requirements, air-conditioning and cooling energy-efficiency requirements, and other EE measures required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts,
  4. Prepare or align the instruments required for e-mobility, including applicable requirements relating to charging infrastructure, technical standards, charging services, electricity supply and tariff arrangements, and other matters required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts, and
  5. Propose the institutional framework and clearly define the roles and responsibilities of the relevant institutions for implementation.

 

6. Qualifications, Tasks, and Level of Effort of Specified Key Experts

The Consultant shall propose a team adequate for the assignment. In its proposal, the Consultant shall specify:

  • Each proposed key personnel position,
  • The name of the proposed expert, where available,
  • Role and responsibilities,
  • Minimum and actual qualifications and detailed relevant experience,
  • Whether the input is international or national/local,
  • Whether the input is home office or field-based,
  • Estimated level of effort in person-days or person-months, and
  • Anticipated timing of deployment and deployment location(s).

At a minimum, the Consultant is expected to consider the inclusion of expertise and an indicative level of effort and split of on-site and remote deployment, as follows:

7. Fees and Reimbursable Expenses

As this engagement will be structured as a lump-sum contract, the selected Consultant shall submit a financial proposal (in addition to a technical proposal) that includes:

  • A total lump-sum price for the performance of the services, payable against the deliverables set out in Section VIII, supported by a breakdown of professional fees by each proposed expert and personnel category, indicating the applicable unit rates and estimated level of effort (person-months or person-days), provided for information purposes; and
  • Reimbursable expenses, included within the lump-sum price, covering any anticipated travel, accommodation, per diem, logistics, communications, and other project-related costs necessary for the performance of the services.

The lump-sum price shall be inclusive of all costs necessary for the performance of the services. The Consultant shall clearly state the assumptions underlying the proposed costs and provide sufficient detail to allow MEC to assess the reasonableness of the proposed budget.

8. Deliverables

The project has six (6) main deliverables.

 

The Consultant shall prepare and submit the following deliverables in accordance with the Scope of Services. The Task references identify the principal Tasks contributing to each deliverable and shall not limit the Consultant's obligation to take into account relevant findings and recommendations arising from other Tasks.

  1. Deliverable 1: Inception Report (Linked to: Tasks 1 to 7)

The Consultant shall submit an Inception Report confirming its understanding of the assignment, methodology, work plan, stakeholder engagement arrangements, data and information requirements, and detailed schedule for carrying out the seven Tasks and submitting the required deliverables.

An Inception Workshop shall be conducted with MEC, NEA, and other relevant stakeholders, and agreed outcomes shall be reflected in the final Inception Report.

The Deliverable shall be submitted within two weeks of Notice to Proceed (NTP).

  1. Deliverable 2: Diagnostic Assessment and Implementation Roadmap (Linked to: Tasks 1, 2 and 3)

The Consultant shall prepare a consolidated Diagnostic Assessment and Implementation Roadmap for the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, relating to renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility.

The deliverable shall consolidate the diagnostic and strategic reviews, identify and categorize the principal implementation, policy, regulatory, and institutional gaps and misalignments, and establish a prioritized, time-bound roadmap to address them.

The roadmap shall identify responsible institutions, required actions, sequencing, dependencies, priorities, and the policies, regulations, codes, and guidelines to be prepared or aligned under this assignment.

The Deliverable shall be submitted within ten weeks of the NTP.

  1. Deliverable 3: Institutional and Capacity Development Framework (Linked to: Task 4 and relevant institutional findings from Tasks 1 to 3)

The Consultant shall prepare an Institutional and Capacity Development Framework setting out the recommended institutional arrangements, roles and responsibilities, coordination arrangements, manpower and skills requirements, identified capacity gaps, and capacity-development strategy for RE, EE and e-mobility.

The proposed framework shall be consistent with the findings and priorities established under Deliverable 2

The Deliverable shall be submitted within eighteen weeks of the NTP.

  1. Deliverable 4: Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework and RE Report (Linked to: Task 5)

The Consultant shall prepare the Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for monitoring progress in RE, EE and e-mobility, including the recommended database, data collection, validation and reporting arrangements and institutional responsibilities.

The deliverable shall include the recommended database and reporting arrangements and the first RE Report, prepared in a form suitable for subsequent updating by NEA.

The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-four weeks of the NTP.

  1. Deliverable 5: Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations (Linked to: Task 6)

The Consultant shall prepare a stand-alone Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations Report, presenting the assessment, findings, and recommended tariff and regulatory pathway in accordance with Task 6.

The deliverable shall provide the analytical and regulatory basis necessary to support tariff-related decisions and the preparation or implementation of the applicable tariff and billing regulatory framework.

The deliverable shall also include the updated tariff model in editable form, covering all MEC-served systems including Ebeye, and concise briefing notes setting out the rationale and supporting calculations for the recommended tariff positions, for use by MEC and NEA in policy and stakeholder discussions.

The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-six weeks of the NTP.

  1. Deliverable 6: Policies, Regulations, Codes and Guidelines for Implementation of the Energy Act (Linked to: Task 7, informed by Tasks 1, 2 and 3)

Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap, the Consultant shall prepare and/or align the policies, regulations, codes, and guidelines identified as necessary to implement the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, within the scope of the assignment.

The deliverable shall comprise the agreed package of new and/or revised policies, regulations, codes and guidelines covering, as applicable:

  • Electricity-sector regulation;
  • Renewable energy;
  • Energy efficiency, including air-conditioning and cooling; and
  • E-mobility.

The policies, regulations, codes and guidelines shall be consistent with the gaps, priorities and sequencing established through the preceding Tasks and agreed with NEA and MEC.

The Deliverable shall be submitted within thirty-two weeks of the NTP.

 9. Contract Duration

The contract duration is 9 months. The expected start date is January 2027. 

10. Evaluation Criteria

The Consultant will be selected using the Consultant’s Qualifications-Based Selection (CQS) method in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and the REGAIN Procurement Plan. Interested firms shall submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) demonstrating their qualifications and relevant experience. EOIs will be evaluated against the criteria below. The most qualified and experienced firm will be invited to submit a combined technical and financial proposal and, if responsive, to negotiate a contract.

  • Experience preparing energy-sector legal, policy and regulatory frameworks, or implementation plans for energy legislation, including regulations, codes and licensing (35 points)
  • Experience in electricity tariff, cost-of-service and revenue-requirement studies for small island or multi-system utilities, preferably with high renewable energy penetration (25 points)
  • Experience in the Pacific or other Small Island Developing States (25 points)
  • Technical and managerial capability of the firm, including core business, years in business, organization and availability of relevant expertise (15 points)

Total: 100 points

Key experts will not be evaluated at the EOI stage. The qualifications of the proposed key experts set out in Section 6 will be reviewed when the selected firm submits its technical proposal.

11. Inputs to be provided by MEC and NEA

MEC, as the Employer, and NEA, as the technical and regulatory counterpart, shall provide or facilitate timely access to the information, documents, data, personnel, and stakeholders reasonably required for the performance of the Services, to the extent available.

NEA shall:

  • Provide or facilitate access to applicable policies, regulations, codes, guidelines, regulatory instruments, sector targets, reports, databases and other relevant regulatory information,
  • Provide available information on institutional arrangements, regulatory processes, staffing and capacity relevant to the assignment,
  • Facilitate access to relevant officials and stakeholders for consultations and workshops, and
  • Review and provide timely technical comments and acceptance of deliverables submitted to it for review or acceptance.

MEC shall:

  • Provide or facilitate access to relevant technical, operational, customer, commercial, financial and investment information and data, including information required for the tariff review, covering all MEC-served systems including Ebeye (former KAJUR operations), and MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model,
  • Provide available plans, studies, reports, databases and information relating to existing and planned RE, EE, e-mobility, storage, and network,
  • Facilitate access to relevant MEC and PMU personnel and stakeholder consultations, and
  • Undertake the contractual, administrative and financial review and approval of deliverables in accordance with the implementation arrangements.

The Consultant shall, as part of the Inception Report, submit a consolidated data and information request specifying the information required, its proposed source, format and required date. The Consultant shall promptly identify material data gaps and propose appropriate alternative sources, assumptions or methodologies where required.

The provision of information by MEC, NEA or any other stakeholder shall not relieve the Consultant of its responsibility for the verification, analysis, adequacy and quality of the Services and deliverables required under the Contract.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Project Engineer

 

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT
